Will Ben Simmons Actually Shoot This Season?

Early in his career, Ben Simmons' aversion to jump shots severely limited his impact. By his last few years prior to the 2025-26 hiatus, that aversion extended to shots of all kinds, including layups.

So, after taking an entire season off, can we have any confidence that that trend will reverse?

Jump shots in training camp are nice. We've seen plenty of a similar vintage in social media videos, but it's never translated to the games. If he suddenly finds the confidence to let it fly, it would genuinely be one of the more shocking possible developments of this upcoming season.

articles.title: New Jalen Duren Rumors on Sign-and-Trade Landing Spots amid Pistons Contract Standoff
articles.summary: The Sacramento Kings and Milwaukee Bucks have interest in a sign-and-trade with the Detroit Pistons for restricted free agent and All-Star center Jalen Duren if Detroit and the 6'10", 250-pound man cannot reach terms on a contract agreement, per Chris Mannix of Sports Illustrated.
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings and Milwaukee Bucks have interest in a sign-and-trade with the Detroit Pistons for restricted free agent and All-Star center Jalen Duren if Detroit and the 6'10", 250-pound man cannot reach terms on a contract agreement, per Chris Mannix of Sports Illustrated.

"Here's what it will take: Money, and more of it than the $200 million the Pistons are reportedly willing to pay Duren over the next five seasons. Clearly, Duren and his representatives believe there is more cash out there. Sacramento and Milwaukee have interest in Duren, a source confirmed, and likely would plus-up the offer if Detroit was willing to play ball on a sign-and-trade."

NBA Reveals 'Points of Emphasis' for Refs

Duren rejected the Detroit Pistons' five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer, and he is not attending their training camp , which began Tuesday.

Duren, who turns 23 on Nov. 18, is entering his fifth NBA season. He has played all four of his pro campaigns with the Pistons, who selected him with the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NBA draft.

Last year, Duren enjoyed a breakout season, averaging 19.5 points on 65.0 percent shooting and 10.5 rebounds en route to helping guide Detroit to a 60-win season and first place in the Eastern Conference standings. It was a tremendous regular season for the Pistons and Duren, who played an instrumental role in quickly turning a team around that won just 14 games in 2023-24.

Unfortunately, the playoffs were tough for the Pistons and Duren. Detroit needed seven games to beat the No. 8 seed Orlando Magic and then fell to the No. 4 seed Cleveland Cavaliers in the second round. Duren's numbers dropped to 10.5 points on 51.4 percent shooting and 8.5 boards per game.

At this point, it's unclear what Duren's future in Detroit will be. Right now, there's a Thursday deadline on the Pistons' one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer to the center. Per Arthur Hill of Hoops Rumors, the Pistons can agree to extend their deadline, but he will stay an RFA if the qualifying offer expires.

There's more than money involved here, though, per a report from ESPN's Eric Woodyard .

"Duren's representatives have made it clear to the Pistons that the standoff is no longer about the money.

"Duren feels disrespected by the process, sources said, particularly compared to how the team handled the contract extension of forward Ausar Thompson, who agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise earlier this month, along with weight clauses in earlier offers.

"The Pistons believe they've made a fair offer to Duren, which is more than he'd make under the qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next offseason. But Duren would be leaving at least $190 million in guaranteed money on the table, as it stands, and would need a max deal next summer to break even over the five years compared with what the Pistons are offering."

It doesn't seem like an answer on this standoff is imminent. The Kings and Bucks are reportedly waiting in the wings if Detroit decides to pursue a sign-and-trade, but the time to watch right now is Thursday at 11:59 p.m. ET, when the deadline on the Pistons' qualifying offer expires.

articles.title: Klay Thompson Reacts to 'Very, Very Hard' 1st Practice with Heat After Joining Giannis, Bam

articles.body:
Miami Heat guard Klay Thompson offered an honest assessment of his first training camp practice with his new team in comments to reporters Tuesday.

Thompson is in town on a two-year, $11.5 million contract after agreeing to a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks and signing as a free agent in Miami.

Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reported on Sept. 22 that Thompson is the "leading candidate" to start at shooting guard.

Thompson enters his 14th NBA season after 12 years with the Golden State Warriors and two with the Dallas Mavericks. Thompson starred on Golden State as one of the league's best shooters, winning four NBA titles and making five All-Star teams (plus two All-NBA teams).

The prolific three-point shooter has made 40.9 percent of his shots beyond the arc over his career, and he's still faring well from deep, making 38.3 percent of his threes last season.

Thompson joins a new-look Heat team that added Milwaukee Bucks superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo into the mix alongside Miami big man Bam Adebayo to form a phenomenal frontcourt on paper. Shooting guard Tim Hardaway Jr. and power forward Bobby Portis Jr. are also in the mix.

Miami will begin its regular season on Oct. 21 at home vs. the Minnesota Timberwolves.

articles.title: Joel Embiid Opens 76ers Camp Without Restrictions, Nick Nurse Talks LeBron James Maintenance Plan
articles.summary: This could finally be the year that Philadelphia 76ers star center Joel Embiid stays healthy.
articles.body:
This could finally be the year that Philadelphia 76ers star center Joel Embiid stays healthy.

After playing in fewer than 40 games in each of the last three seasons, Embiid is entering training camp without restrictions. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse announced that the 2023 NBA MVP was a full participant in Tuesday's practice and "looked great" after getting into great shape over the summer.

Nurse also told reporters that there have been discussions about managing the workloads of Embiid and star forward LeBron James, and the team is figuring out plans for the rest of the preseason and back-to-backs during the season.

NBA Reveals 'Points of Emphasis' for Refs

Embiid has a lot of work to do to shed his injury-prone label, and he appeared to lose a significant amount of weight during the offseason:

James hyped Embiid's offseason preparation when he spoke with reporters during Monday's media day.

"Jo is one of the most talented guys we have in the world," James told reporters . "… For him, it's all about health. … I see he's put in a lot of work on his body, put in a lot of work on his game, put in a lot of work on his mentals this offseason."

Adding James in free agency propelled the Sixers to the top of the list of title contenders in the Eastern Conference. Philadelphia also acquired star guard Jaylen Brown to pair with the talented backcourt of Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

Still, keeping Embiid healthy could be the key to the Sixers' success. At full strength, the 32-year-old was one of the most dominant forces in the NBA with three straight years averaging at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block from 2021 to 2024.

If Embiid can return to his old form, Philadelphia could finally achieve the deep playoff run that has eluded the team for over two decades.

articles.title: Florida's Denzel Aberdeen Granted Temporary Injunction, Will Be Eligible for 5th CBB Season
articles.summary: A Florida judge granted Denzel Aberdeen an injunction that will allow the guard to play a fifth season of college basketball.
articles.body:
A Florida judge granted Denzel Aberdeen an injunction that will allow the guard to play a fifth season of college basketball.

Aberdeen averaged 13.5 points and 3.4 assists with Kentucky in 2025-26. He transferred back to Florida, where he won a national championship and played for three years, for the upcoming season.

Broncos OL Drug Tested After Viral Clip 🎥

The NCAA Division I Cabinet approved a new rule , which goes into effect in fall 2027, allowing athletes to have five years of eligibility within a five-year period starting from their enrollment.

Current athletes weren't grandfathered in, but some have pursued other means to earn a fifth year for themselves. Aberdeen filed suit against the NCAA earlier this month.

The 6'5" guard initially planned to argue in front of the NCAA that his first year at Florida was effectively a redshirt season. He appeared in 12 games and played a total of 41 minutes.

The "five-for-five" rule provided Aberdeen with a different basis by which to state his case.

Now that Aberdeen's return to Gainesville is confirmed, Florida will strengthen is resume to be No. 1 in the major preseason polls.

The Gators return their top three scorers (Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon and Boogie Fland) along with Rueben Chinyelu, who averaged a double-double (10.9 points and 11.2 rebounds). Aberdeen should make an immediate impact as well given his past experience with coach Todd Golden.

Florida has more depth than any other team and championship experience with some holdovers from its title-winning squad in 2024-25.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Reacts to Praise from LeBron James, NBA Stars After Leading Knicks to Historic Title
articles.summary: New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson appreciates the praise various superstars have given him and his team during media days this week.

New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson appreciates the praise various superstars have given him and his team during media days this week.

Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James gave "much respect" to the Knicks and Brunson during his media day availability, per ESPN's Dave McMenamin , amid comments about why he didn't join New York in free agency (in essence, the Knicks were off the table after they won the championship).

"But much respect to the Knicks, obviously," James said. "An unbelievable team, unbelievable players. Shout out Jalen Brunson. I love that guy, he's unbelievable. But, yeah, I'm happy where I'm at, and I'm looking forward to it."

Miami Heat superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo also shouted out the Knicks and Brunson.

The Knicks just won their first NBA title in 53 years, led by Brunson. The three-time All-NBA guard averaged an NBA-high 28.4 points in the playoffs en route to the NBA Finals MVP award. New York also went 16-3 in the playoffs, including victories in 15 of its last 16 games.

articles.title: Xavi Pascual da de su propia medicina a sus ex del Barça
articles.standfirst: Punter (25+5+2) no basta para salvar a los azulgranas, que regalan el partido en un segundo cuarto lamentable (29-12)
articles.summary: Punter (25+5+2) no basta para salvar a los azulgranas, que regalan el partido en un segundo cuarto lamentable (29-12)
articles.body: El Dubai Basketball sometió al Barcelona (94-87) haciendo gala de sus múltiples argumentos ofensivos ante un rival que acabó en la lona en el segundo cuarto con un parcial de 29-12 (52-37) y que luego no fue capaz de levantar pese a los esfuerzos de Kevin Punter (25+5+2), principal representante del antiguo régimen azulgrana. Nuevos tiempos para un equipo al que le queda mucho para ensamblar un puzzle con demasiadas piezas nuevas. Xavi Pascual, ahora en el banquillo del Dubai, demostró a sus ex que su catálogo del baloncesto no se limita a reducir a sus rivales con una defensa furibunda, como algunos creían, y que cuando hay que dar rienda suelta al atauque porque tiene jugadores para hacerlo, permite que su equipo se desmelene aunque no apriete tanto atrás. Teniendo a tipos como Kabengele (21+6), Bacon (14+7) o Wright (14+2+3) se lo puede permitir su equipo, que perdió la batalla de las pérdidas (15-5), pero ganó la del rebote (34-27). El inicio del partido fue un intercambio de golpes brutal. El Barça comenzó disparado con los triples de Parra y Robinson (2-8), pero el Dubai respondió con dos de Wright y uno de Bacon para voltear el marcador (10-13). Luego fue Kabengele quien contrarrestó las embestidas de Punter y Gibson. Y Balcerowsky y Umude pusieron el contrapunto a los arreones de Walkup y Blossomgame antes del final de un primer cuarto de locos (23-25). Todos tiraban y todos metían. Todo cambió en el segundo acto, cuando el Dubai siguió castigando el aro azulgrana mientras al Barça se le hacía de noche en ataque. Shengelia, Diakite y Mintz comandaron un 12-1 para cimentar la escapada local (35-26, min 14). Y luego fueron Walkup, Petrusev y un Kabengele omnipresente quienes pusieron la máxima renta para los de Pascual al descanso (52-37). El segundo cuarto azulgrana fue lastimoso, con un 29-12 (4/14 t2 y 1/8 triples). Era difícil jugar peor y con menos acierto, y aunque en la reanudación apuntaba a más de lo mismo con una nueva máxima para el Dubai (56-39) el Barça por fin sacó la cabeza del fango. Lo hizo con un parcial de 0-8 fabricado con triples de Punter y Gibson más una canasta de este último (56-47, min 24). Pero duró poco la alegría de los azulgranas, lo que tardaron en entrar los triples de Bacon y Kabengele y los tiros de Wright y Blossomgame, que sepultaron por las bravas el conato de reacción culé reduciéndolo a un breve espejismo (76-56, min 29). Dos canastas de Martin y una de Punter alimentaron las esperanzas del Barça antes del último acto (76-62, min 30). Bertans parecía consolidar la brecha local con un triple (79-64, min 31), pero Punter volvió a hacer la goma parta su equipo liderando un parcial de 2-9 con siete puntos seguidos (81-73, min 34). Kabengele, imparable cerca y lejos del aro, anotó un triple para frenar la sangría (84-73). Pero dos canastas de Balcerowski y un triple de Martin volvieron a resucitar al Barça (86-80, min 37). Wright y Okobo dieron oxígeno a los de Pascual (90-80), pero Punter, el de siempre, permitió soñar al Barça primero con una canasta (90-84) que fue enjugada por Kabengele, y luego con un triple (92-87, a 24 segundos del final), hasta que Okobo sentenció con dos tiros libres (94-87). 94 - Dubai (23+29+24+18): Wright (14), Okobo (9), Bacon (14), Blossongame (10), Kabengele (21) -cinco inicial- Diakite (7), Shengelia (4), Walkup (5), Bertans (3), Mintz (3) y Petrusev (4). 87 - Barça (25+12+25+25): Punter (25), Robinson (7), Minaya (), Parra (8), Balcerowski (10) -cinco inicial- Brizuela (0), Umude (8), Gibson (12), Martin (9) y Nkamhoua (8). Árbitros: Olegs Latisevs (LET), Piotr Pastusiak (POL), Gentian Cici (ALB). Sin eliminados. articles.title: New Karl-Anthony Towns Rumors Reveal Stance on Knicks' Proposed Pay Cut amid Contract Talks
articles.summary: New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns is reportedly willing to follow in star point guard Jalen Brunson's footsteps as he seeks a contract extension, but only to a point.
articles.body:
New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns is reportedly willing to follow in star point guard Jalen Brunson's footsteps as he seeks a contract extension, but only to a point.

On Tuesday's episode of NBA Today , ESPN's Malika Andrews reported that Towns "is also willing to take a pay cut, but the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Brunson set a precedent when he signed a four-year, $156.5 million contract extension in the 2024 offseason, $113 million less than the five-year, $269.1 million deal he would've received if he had waited a year to sign a new deal. His unselfishness paid off, as the Knicks were able to build a championship roster that won the franchise's first title since 1973.

Towns is eligible for a four-year contract extension worth over $276 million. Under his current deal, he is set to make $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for next season.

During Monday's media day, Towns declared that he wants to remain in New York on a long-term deal.

"I've made it known I want to play here," Towns told reporters . "I've been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done and step on the floor and feel as comfortable as possible."

When asked if he would be comfortable with continuing contract discussions after the 2026-27 season starts next month, Towns said, "In this situation, there's no comfortability to be had."

The Knicks appear determined to remain under the second apron, so Towns likely will have to settle for a compromise if he wants to secure a long-term extension.

articles.title: El debut de Nick Smith Jr. no impide otro tropiezo del Real Madrid en la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, lastrados por las pérdidas (21) y la pésima tarde de Luwawu-Cabarrot (-10 de valoración), sucumben ante el Anadolu Efes de Pablo Laso
articles.summary: Los blancos, lastrados por las pérdidas (21) y la pésima tarde de Luwawu-Cabarrot (-10 de valoración), sucumben ante el Anadolu Efes de Pablo Laso
articles.body: Todavía no arranca el Real Madrid en la Euroliga. En su visita al Anadolu Efes de Pablo Laso sumó su segunda derrota en dos jornadas (94-84). Fue con diferencia el peor partido de los blancos en lo que va de temporada. Lastrados por 21 pérdidas de balón (14 ya al descanso) que se tradujeron en 30 puntos turcos y 27 al contraataque, por un segundo cuarto terrible (23-12) y por otro desenlace lleno de imprecisiones. Todo lo que remaron para tener opciones se fue por el sumidero en un pésimo final. La mejor noticia para el Madrid fue el estreno del deseado Nick Smith Jr., que salió de inicio. Hizo 10 puntos. Se le vio algo desubicado, sobre todo atrás, cargándose con faltas, una flagrante. Le puede costar hacerse a los arbitrajes europeos. Pese a su fama de anotador compulsivo, poco individualista: sólo tres tiros de campo. Promete alegrías al madridismo. Otro de los llamados a ser referentes ofensivos de los blancos, Luwawu-Cabarrot, vivió una tarde aciaga. No se le recuerda nada igual a uno de los mejores anotadores de la Euroliga la temporada pasada: -10 de valoración con 0/5 en tiros, dos pérdidas y tres faltas. Sin la pólvora del francés, fue Campazzo quien lidero el ataque, con 16 puntos. Buen partido también de Okeke, con 11 y 3/5 en triples para mejorar las cifras globales: 9/26, aún lejos de lo deseado. El Madrid no comenzó bien (12-5). Fue la segunda unidad, con Maledon, Jantunen y Okeke, la que le hizo arrancar con un mejor movimiento de balón. A mitad del segundo cuarto aún mandaba por 30-33 tras la primera canasta de Smith. Después cometió una flagrante y, sin que fuera la consecuencia, ahí comenzó el bajonazo madridista. Fue acumulando pérdidas, algunas infantiles. El Efes volaba mientras el Madrid perdía las alas. Dozier (18 puntos), James (12) y Saric (10) eran las amenazas. También buenos minutos de Russell delante y de Kai Jones detrás. Yusta (+15 con él en pista) disfrutó de casi todo el parcial de 20-4 que dejó tocado al Madrid (50-37). Dominar el rebote no le servía de nada. Al descanso, 14 pérdidas que aprovechó el Efes con 23 puntos y 17 a la contra. Los triples con los que el Madrid volvió de vestuarios tampoco bastaron. El Efes alcanzó el +14 (67-53) con un acierto de Dozier tras una gran circulación. Pedro Martínez apostó por un quinteto pequeño con Jantunen y Okeke por dentro. La distancia se fue recortando. Centímetro a centímetro, los blancos recuperaron opciones al final del tercer cuarto (72-65). Pese a los tapones de Kai Jones, Okeke falló un triple para el -1 y con 84-80 comenzó la sucesión de errores. Después de controlar las pérdidas durante casi toda la segunda parte, llegó una de Campazzo ante James. Luego, una falta de ataque de Tavares. Un rebote ofensivo concedido fue la condena final. Strazel, con cuatro tiros libres, sentenció y con una última bandeja abrió más la herida. El Madrid no arranca en Europa. Este jueves, en Sofía, contra el Hapoel Tel Aviv, en busca de la primera victoria. Conviene no perder más terreno. 94 - Anadolu Efes (27+26+19+22): James (12), Strazel (14), Dozier (18), Saric (10) y Fernando (8) -cinco inicial-, Loyd (12), Yusta (3), Russell (5), Malcolm (2), Osmani (5) y Jones (5). 84 - Real Madrid (29+12+24+19): Campazzo (16), Smith Jr (10), Deck (2), Pradilla (4) y Tavares (8) -cinco inicial-, Luwawu-Cabarrot (-), Abalde (3), Okeke (11), Maledon (9), Jantunen (7), Feliz (10) y Jones (4). Árbitros: Milan Nedovic (SLO), Saulius Racys (LTU), Vasiliki Tsaroucha (GRE). Señalaron falta disruptiva a Matthew Strazel (min.6), del Anadolu Efes, y flagrante a Nick Smith Jr., del Real Madrid (min.13). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: Partido de la seguda jornada de la Euroliga disputado en el Turkcell Basketball Development Center de Estambul (Turquía).

articles.title: LeBron James is reportedly paying $330,000 to fly from New York to the Sixers' practice
articles.summary: LeBron James has played in Cleveland, Miami, and Los Angeles. He has won four MVPs and a bunch of rings.
articles.body: LeBron James has played in Cleveland, Miami, and Los Angeles. He has won four MVPs and a bunch of rings. At 42, in his 24th season, he now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers. And he has decided that the one thing he will not do is live in Philadelphia. This week, ESPN's Dave McMenamin heard a loud helicopter outside the Sixers' practice facility after Tuesday's practice. It was waiting to fly LeBron to New York. That's how you know the rumor is real.LeBron James Is Paying About $330,000 a Season to Not Move to PhiladelphiaTo understand this, you have to know LeBron's history with New York. Fortune noted that he toured his first Manhattan apartment more than 15 years ago. He has always loved playing at Madison Square Garden, and the Knicks showed interest this summer, but the deal never happened.So he took the next best thing: a two-year deal with the Sixers, a team with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe. And he kept New York for himself. He told ESPN he will move between "multiple residences" in Philadelphia and New York.The trip is about 100 miles and takes roughly 45 minutes. The reported price is about $4,000 each way, so one round trip is about $8,000.Our math: 41 home games × $8,000 = about $328,000. This is our estimate. It counts home games only, so practices and shootarounds would push it higher. And the $4,000 is a reported price, not a bill we have seen.The part fans are nervous aboutFans love LeBron and want him on the ground. Replies begged him to take a train or drive. Others said helicopters are safe. There is a reason for the worry. The 2020 helicopter crash that killed Kobe Bryant and eight others was caused by fog, and fog is common in the New York-to-Philadelphia corridor, especially in the mornings. New York also restricts helicopters heavily because of noise and safety rules. We have no report of any problem with LeBron's flights. This is the context fans are reacting to, and nothing more.It's not really about money. $328,000 is small for a player of his level. It's about a man who spent two decades in a spotlight and finally picked one thing that is only for him. Some athletes buy an island. LeBron bought a commute. And honestly? articles.title: NBA reportedly close to selecting winning bid for Las Vegas expansion team, has 3 finalist groups
articles.summary: The deal, which will include a new arena in the city, is expected to be worth at least $12 billion.
articles.body:
The NBA appears to be close to selecting a winning bid for the owner of the Las Vegas expansion team.

The NBA is expected to select the winning bid "in the very near future," according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The deal, which will include a new arena in the city, is expected to be worth at least $12 billion. A specific timeline is not yet known.

There are reportedly three finalist groups in place: The first is led by Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; the second by Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; and the third is a group led by Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo.

Nancy Walton Laurie is the daughter of Walmart co-founder James Walton. Her husband, Bill, used to own the NHL's St.Louis Blues. The couple already has a home in the Las Vegas area and an estimated net worth of more than $17 billion, according to Forbes . The Walton family is part of the ownership group of the NFL's Denver Broncos, too.

Lasry is the former co-owner of the Milwaukee Bucks , though he sold his stake in the team to Jimmy and Dee Haslam at a $3.5 billion valuation in 2023. He would be a partner in the group led by Apostolopoulos, a Canadian billionaire who attempted to purchase both the Charlotte Hornets and NFL's Washington Commanders.

Colangelo is the former owner of the Phoenix Suns . The Hall of Famer, who also was the longtime managing director of USA Basketball, sold the Suns in 2004 for a then-record $401 million. He's currently the chairman of the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame.

Colangelo is teaming up with Foley, who owns the NHL's Las Vegas Golden Knights and AFC Bournemouth in the Premier League. Foley paid a $500 million expansion fee for the Golden Knights when they entered the NHL in 2017. Colangelo's Las Vegas Jacks group is on board, too, which includes former Turner Sports president David Levy, Scott Colangelo and others.

The NBA has been looking into expansion for years now, and has confirmed that both Las Vegas and Seattle are the two frontrunner cities. The $12 billion price tag Charania reported Tuesday is in line with the most recent sale of an NBA franchise. The Los Angeles Lakers were sold last month for a record $12.5 billion to a group led by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger. That made it the most expensive sports franchise sale in North America .

While the Las Vegas team appears to be close to coming together, the status of a future Seattle franchise — which would presumably revive the SuperSonics — is still unknown. Regardless of when both teams come together and officially enter the league, Tuesday's report is a significant step in the process.

articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "Tuvimos opciones de remontar, pero las pérdidas al final nos mataron"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la segunda derrota de su equipo en la Euroliga
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la segunda derrota de su equipo en la Euroliga
articles.body: Pedro Martínez, entrenador del Real Madrid, señaló este martes que las pérdidas de balón, especialmente en la primera parte y en los minutos finales, "mataron" las esperanzas de remontada del equipo, que pese a tener opciones, acabó cayendo por 94-84 ante el Anadolu Efes en Estambul. El Real Madrid llegó a estar a solo cuatro puntos en los minutos finales, pero las 21 pérdidas de balón, 14 de ellas en la primera mitad, fueron una losa que pesó demasiado. "Hicimos un gran esfuerzo en el segundo tiempo. El problema es que en el primer tiempo tuvimos muchas pérdidas. Luego estuvimos mejor, aunque las pérdidas al final nos mataron. Tuvimos buena mentalidad para remontar, pero necesitamos mejorar, especialmente a la hora de compartir el balón", dijo Martínez a los micrófonos de la Euroliga tras el partido. Ya en la rueda de prensa, reiteró el agujero de las pérdidas, aunque valoró la mejora de mentalidad de sus jugadores en el segundo tiempo. "Jugamos 13 o 14 minutos en la dirección correcta en la primera parte, pero luego cometimos pérdidas que permitieron puntos fáciles del Efes y que provocaron una gran ventaja en los últimos cinco minutos del segundo cuarto, haciéndonos difícil competir. En la segunda parte tuvimos una mejor mentalidad, defendimos mejor y limitamos las pérdidas. Tuvimos opciones a dos minutos del final tras una gran remontada, pero otra vez, las pérdidas y sus buenos ataques decidieron el partido para el Efes", analizó. Preguntado por si parte de las pérdidas fueron por la defensa del Efes en situaciones de "corte Iverson", un sistema ofensivo, se centró en las situaciones que sus propios jugadores pueden mejorar. "Necesitamos analizar cómo cometimos las pérdidas. Puede que algunas fueran en situaciones específicas en esta situación, pero en general creo que no fue nuestro problema. Perdimos balones en situaciones sencillas, con ventaja...Creo que hay que pensar en qué podemos mejorar en las situaciones que entrenamos, pero no es esta situación en particular", concluyó.

articles.summary: El Roig Arena volvió a disfrutar de la actuación coral de su equipo que recordó al de la temporada pasada y registra su partido más anotador en Euroliga ante los de Galbiati
articles.body: Llegaba Valencia Basket con alguna duda tras el debut con derrota en casa en Liga Endesa, pero los de Xavi Albert volvieron a utilizar la Euroliga para disfrutar en el estreno del Roig Arena. Y lo hicieron como si no hubiera pasado una temporada, con una versión que se asemejó mucho a la que maravilló la campaña pasada. Los taronja sacaron del mapa a Baskonia (111-88) y colocaron el 2-0 en la tabla clasificatoria. El partido estuvo igualado durante los primeros cinco minutos, con un intercambio de canastas entre ambos equipos, pero un 10-0 de parcial entre Sako, Osetkowski y Puerto ubicaron una diferencia (19-8) que Baskonia no pudo estrechar en ningún momento. Valencia Basket se marchó tras los primeros 10 minutos con un 26-10 demoledor. Una actuación conjunta de los naranjas colocó el 42-17 en el segundo cuarto que hacía presagiar lo peor para los vitorianos, que consiguió maquillar el cuarto para marcharse a vestuarios a una distancia similar (52-33). Tras el parón, Valencia no quitó el pie del acelerador y un inspirado Armoni Brooks no permitía a los visitantes acercarse en el marcador. 17 puntos y cuatro triples para el escolta estadounidense que vivió su primera gran noche en el Roig Arena. Un torrente de juego ofensivo que se apoyó en el doble-doble de TJ Shorts, con 12 puntos y 10 asistencias. El base volvió a ser el líder del equipo. En el último periodo, un triple de Mirotic puso la máxima del partido (94-65) a falta de siete minutos para finalizar el partido, y en el pabellón ya sobrevolaba la idea de superar su partido con más puntos anotados en la competición europea (108, precisamente ante Baskonia el pasado febrero). Finalmente, Osetkowski anotó otro triple casi sobre la bocina para terminar de redondear una gran noche en Valencia y establecer en 111 el nuevo récord anotador. Hasta siete jugadores taronjas anotaron dobles dígitos ante un Baskonia muy mermado en el que Sedekerskis, Faried, Stewart y Lawson dejaron una buena carta de tiro, pero sobre el que Paolo Galbiati tendrá que seguir trabajando para volver a consolidar un nuevo proyecto. articles.title: ‘Numbers Don’t Lie’ — 3-Time WNBA Champion Calls Out ‘Clickbait’ Media Coverage of Angel Reese, Caitlin Clark, and Co.
articles.summary: The WNBA has enjoyed a surge in popularity over the last few years, with that growth accelerating following the arrivals of Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese in...
articles.body:
The WNBA has enjoyed a surge in popularity over the last few years, with that growth accelerating following the arrivals of Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese in 2024 and Paige Bueckers in 2025.

Now, former WNBA star and three-time champion Swin Cash has shared her thoughts on media scrutiny surrounding women's sports amid the league's rising popularity.

WNBA Champion Swin Cash Calls Out 'Clickbait' Coverage Amid Women's Basketball Boom

Cash, the second overall pick of the 2002 WNBA draft, reflected on the growth of women's sports while appearing on "Beyond The Curve" on the Scripps Sports Network .

The WNBA legend-turned-media figure weighed in on the media coverage of the WNBA and its biggest athletes. She lamented that the media sometimes focuses on negative stories amid the league's ever-rising popularity.

"There are so many rich stories. There are media people, who just aren't media and it's clickbait. That is the direction you have to go in. But if you're authentically loving the sport, we understand and I always say this, 'Men lie, women lie; numbers don't lie,'" Cash told Olympic gold medalist Sanya Richards-Ross. Cash, who has been mentioned in recent reports as a potential candidate to succeed WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert, added that it was the media's responsibility to tell athletes' stories in an "authentic way" rather than resorting to clickbait.

"The numbers for women's sports are going up because people love watching the play on the field. And it's up to us that are now in the media and have these chairs to tell the stories in a very authentic way and not just clickbait," she added. The WNBA has faced a string of off-court controversies this year, with Clark and other players dealing with online abuse and heightened scrutiny amid the league's growing media spotlight. MORE: 'Poorly Constructed Roster' – Fever Radio Analyst Sounds Alarm On 1 Major Weakness With Indiana On the Brink Of Playoffs Exit vs. Aces The league's rise has also coincided with heightened debate, with several players reporting severe abuse on social media. Amid the string of controversies surrounding the WNBA, commissioner Cathy Engelbert has faced significant criticism this year. In July, 11 House Republicans sent the WNBA a letter raising concerns about Caitlin Clark's treatment on the court and calling for greater accountability over player safety. On Sept. 4, the 61-year-old announced that she would retire from her role at the end of the year.

articles.title: Walker Kessler Predicts Lakers Will Be 'Nasty Defensive Team' on Video Ahead of 2026-27 NBA Season

Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler believes that the team will be one of the NBA's elite defensive units during the 2026-27 season.

"I think we're gonna be a nasty defensive team," Kessler told reporters Tuesday. "I'm just being honest, seeing these guys hound the ball on the perimeter."

"We're gonna be really good defensively," he added. "We have a lot of defensive tools."

What NBA's Vegas expansion team is going to cost

Los Angeles wasn't known for its ability to slow down opponents last year, ranking No. 20 among all teams with a 115.5 defensive rating (via NBA.com ).

While Lakers stars Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves aren't known for their defensive acumen, Kessler was one of several offseason additions that their front office made to improve as a two-way squad.

Kessler is entering his first season in Los Angeles after a four-year stint with the Utah Jazz, establishing himself as one of the league's top rim protectors. He owns a career average of 2.4 blocks per game.

While Kessler was limited to just five appearances last season due to shoulder surgery , he suited up in 58 games during his 2024-25 campaign.

That year, opponents shot just 49.0 percent from the field against him within six feet of the basket (via NBA.com ). It ranked No. 7 among all players to appear in at least 40 contests.

The Lakers will also be looking to improve their on-ball defense, attempting to do so by bringing active perimeters defenders such as Matisse Thybulle and Quentin Grimes into the mix.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Reveals Blazers Starting Lineup Plans Amid Role Debate After Ja Morant Trade
articles.summary: Damian Lillard weighed in on the Portland Trail Blazers' new starting lineup following the offseason addition of Ja Morant.
articles.body:
Damian Lillard weighed in on the Portland Trail Blazers' new starting lineup following the offseason addition of Ja Morant.

According to Jason Quick of The Athletic, Lillard said Tuesday that "as far as I know, Ja will start, I will start and Deni will start … that's as far as I know."

Lillard also revealed that he hasn't discussed Portland's lineup as well as his starting role with Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori yet, per Quick.

What NBA's Vegas expansion team is going to cost

Portland acquired Morant from the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for forwards Jerami Grant and Kris Murray on June 29.

Morant previously spent seven years in Memphis, averaging 22.4 points and 7.4 assists per game while earning two All-Star nods during his tenure with the organization.

He started in 325 of his 327 games played on the Grizzlies.

Still, Morant has expressed a willingness to operate in a bench role with the Trail Blazers.

"I think winning is the most important thing for me," Morant told reporters on Monday. "So whatever role I have to play to get that done, I don't think anybody would be mad after a win. As a starter, if I'm starting, if I'm not, it's the same thing. It's day one right now, I feel like that's coach's questions, but for me I have no problem with either."

Morant and Lillard are both new additions to Portland's rotation, as the latter missed the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn Achilles .

The Trail Blazers still finished with a 42-40 record and advanced to the playoffs led by Deni Avdija, who earned his first career All-Star nod. Jrue Holiday, Shaedon Sharpe and Scoot Henderson all started in Portland's backcourt throughout the year.

If Lillard and Morant start alongside Avdija, the Trail Blazers have two spots left in their opening lineup. Center Donovan Clingan is back in the mix, while defensive-minded forward Toumani Camara is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he started all 82 games.

Portland will open the 2026-27 regular season against the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Makes History as Fever Stay Alive vs. Aces, Box Score Stats, Highlights for A'ja, More
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever aren't done yet.
articles.body:
Facing elimination in the best-of-three first-round series, the Fever downed the Las Vegas Aces 99-89 behind a historic performance from Caitlin Clark.

The Aces had control early, jumping out to an 11-point lead early in the second quarter, but a run fueled by Clark's scoring and passing helped Indiana trim the lead and eventually head into halftime up five.

Clark finished the first half with 14 points and 11 assists, making her the first player in WNBA history to record a double-double with points and assists in the first half of a playoff game.

The Fever kept their momentum heading into the second half and managed to jump ahead 72-60 heading into the final quarter. Indiana shut down Aces star A'ja Wilson in the third, allowing no points from the four-time MVP.

But the defending champs didn't go away after going down by double digits. With Jackie Young carrying the load on offense, Las Vegas cut the lead down to just five points halfway through the fourth quarter.

Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell responded to Young's run with one of their own, and it was quickly a double-digit lead once again for the Fever. Amid the run from Indiana, the Aces lost even more momentum when Wilson was assessed a technical foul after an interaction with a fan.

Indiana's offense took a blow when Clark fouled out with just under three minutes remaining, and the Aces made another late push to get back into it, trimming the lead to five points.

But Boston put the Fever back up seven, and a pair of free throws from Sophie Cunningham on the following possession extended the lead to nine with just over a minute to play.

It was ultimately too big a deficit for Las Vegas to overcome, and Indiana iced the game at the free-throw line.

After the win for the Fever, the first round will head back to Las Vegas, where the Aces will look to answer with a series-clinching win.

articles.title: Updated WNBA Playoff Bracket Picture 2026 After Liberty Eliminate Lynx, Fever Beat Aces
articles.summary: Elimination was on the table Tuesday during a pair of Game 2s in the 2026 WNBA playoffs.
articles.body:
Elimination was on the table Tuesday during a pair of Game 2s in the 2026 WNBA playoffs.

First, the reigning-champion Las Vegas Aces had an opportunity to eliminate Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever after winning the first contest at home. Then, the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx had their backs against the wall after dropping the first game to the New York Liberty.

Indiana Fever def. Las Vegas Aces, 99-89 (Series tied, 1-1)

New York Liberty def. Minnesota Lynx, 87-71 (NY wins series, 2-0)

The three-time All-Star was unstoppable and led the Fever to a 99-89 victory over A'ja Wilson and the Aces to even the series at a game apiece. She made history as the first WNBA player to record a double-double with points and assists in a playoff half and finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds.

While she was the star, Kelsey Mitchell (26 points) and Aliyah Boston (22 points) provided important support and helped counter an incredible performance from Jackie Young (31 points, five assists and four rebounds) and a near double-double from Wilson (22 points and nine rebounds).

Indiana figured to be the more desperate team out of the gates with its season on the line, but it was actually Las Vegas that seized early momentum and built a double-digit lead with Wilson getting to the line, Chelsea Gray hitting from deep and Young doing a little bit of everything.

The frustration was apparent for the home team when Clark picked up a technical foul, but she also responded in superstar fashion.

The Fever stormed back to take a five-point halftime lead with Clark putting on a show. She connected from deep as usual but also didn't hesitate to attack the lane and get out in transition. That created open looks for her teammates when the Aces collapsed, and Mitchell provided a scoring burst as the dynamic backcourt duo took over for stretches.

Raven Johnson hit a buzzer-beater off Clark's 11th assist in the first half in a fitting finish for a guard-led flurry.

Indiana extended its lead to double digits in the third quarter with Clark continuing to play brilliantly and Boston establishing herself as a scorer to give the home team more of a frontcourt presence.

Of course, having Clark dishing dimes to her made life easier for Boston as she cut into the space created by all the attention the guard drew.

The Aces didn't go down without a fight, though, as Young caught fire and aggressively sought out her shot while cutting the deficit to as low as three in the fourth quarter. While Clark responded with two massive threes to create more breathing room again, she fouled out with fewer than three minutes remaining.

Fortunately for the Fever, they had enough breathing room to put the game away.

The Liberty completed a two-game sweep of the Lynx with a blowout 87-71 victory behind stifling defense and an excellent performance from their three stars. Jonquel Jones (21 points and 13 rebounds), Sabrina Ionescu (18 points and seven assists) and Breanna Stewart (21 points, five rebounds and four assists) were unstoppable and in full control throughout the contest.

Napheesa Collier (14 points and seven rebounds) and Courtney Williams (18 points, eight rebounds and five assists) did what they could for the Lynx, but it was to no avail.

If the Game 1 victory wasn't all the proof fans needed, the start of Tuesday's contest further drove home the point that the Liberty are far from a typical No. 8 seed with so much star power.

It was Stewart who dominated Game 1 with 34 points, but New York used a balanced approach to build a commanding 12-point halftime lead right out of the gates in Game 2. Jones was unguardable inside as a matchup problem for the Lynx frontcourt, while Ionescu hit from deep and facilitated as the lead guard.

Stewart, of course, was also quite involved and did a little bit of everything.

She attacked the basket as a scorer, contributed on the glass, mixed in some assists and even protected the rim as a shot-blocker. The blocks were part of a stout defensive approach for New York, as Minnesota struggled to generate any type of offensive momentum as its season seemed to be slipping away.

It was more of the same in the third quarter, as everything was difficult for the Lynx on the offensive side with Liberty defenders swarming shooters and cutting off driving lanes.

Throw in Ionescu's three-pointers in front of a raucous home crowd, and all the momentum and a 12-point lead was on New York's side heading into the fourth. Suddenly, a Minnesota team that finished with more wins than anyone else in the league this season was staring at a stunning exit without a single playoff victory.

Things went from bad to worse for the Lynx for much of the fourth as well with star guard Olivia Miles on the bench amid a rough shooting performance (1-of-8 from the field) and an offense desperately looking for answers.

Even when it found a temporary one with Aari McDonald and Collier hitting back-to-back jumpers, Ionescu was ready with an answer with an assist to Jones and a driving layup. It reached a point that the final minutes were nothing more than a formality with the Liberty in full control.

articles.title: Transgender athletes have taken 2,293 championship spots from biological women, new research finds
articles.summary: New research found transgender athletes have taken 2,293 championship spots from biological women since the mid-1980s across more than 14,000 events.
articles.body: So ... it's rare, right? That's the argument certain activists keep making when it comes to the debate about trans athletes in female sports. It's not a great position, frankly — because if something is wrong, it doesn't matter how rare it is. It should be stopped, assuming doing so doesn't trigger undue consequences. AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS' But new data suggests that this "uncommon" occurrence isn't so uncommon after all. Recent research from the Concerned Women of America found that transgender athletes have bumped biological women out of 2,293 championship spots since the mid-1980s. This is far different than simply noting the number of transgender athletes in sports. This is pointing out how many biological females would have won a specific honor if not for the trans athlete that took it. For the report, the think tank drew on information compiled by HeCheated.org, a volunteer-operated database that tracks reported instances of trans athletes competing in women's sports. In total, it found that they have partaken in more than 14,000 female sporting events ranging from high school to college to amateur to professional. The HeCheated.org list is extensive. The first page alone has 200 instances ranging from March 27, 2025, to September 18, 2026. It shows examples of biological males making league All-Star teams in high school lacrosse, or winning high school state championships in track and field in Washington, California and Oregon, or earning All-conference recognition in college fencing. There were also a couple of examples of trans athletes receiving "most improved" awards. TRANS TRACK STAR SWEEPS THREE EVENTS, SHARES FIRST-PLACE PODIUM AND QUALIFIES FOR CA STATE MEET YET AGAIN And as long as laws that allow this to happen exist, there is no evidence of this slowing down. Author Abigail Shrier wrote the book "Irreversible Damage" in 2020, in which she noted a 1,000 to 5,000 percent increase in the number of trans-identifying youth over a several-year period. Other research has noted that this uptick has no end in sight. In 2023, the CDC Youth Risk Behavior Survey found that about three percent of high-school students identified as transgender. In 2025, the Williams Institute estimated that 724,000 Americans ages 13–17 identify as transgender, which was roughly equivalent to 3.6 percent. And the Society for Evidence Based Gender Medicine (SEGM) estimated that trans/nonbinary identification for college students is at an all-time high, ranging from 4.7 percent to 6.7 percent. That last number shouldn't affect participation in the NCAA, which requires athletes play on teams that match their sex assigned at birth. But when we're talking about, say, the WNBA, which still doesn't have a concrete rule about gender restrictions, who's to say one of these college kids doesn't try to pull a much-more-subtle Enes Kanter and work their way into the league? US OLYMPIC HERO NANCY HOGSHEAD LAUNCHES PETITION CALLING FOR WNBA TO RESTRICT GENDER ELIGIBILITY When I was at The Seattle Times, I interviewed a high school athlete named Ahnaleigh Wilson, who lost to a boy in a high school track meet when she was in eighth grade. She told me that she had since competed against four biological males in high school. I couldn't confirm that, but when I see research documenting biological males competing in more than 14,000 events involving females, and consider that alongside a UCLA study estimating that as many as 122,000 transgender youth may be competing in high school sports, I tend to believe her. First, they say it's not happening. Then, they say "OK, it's happening, but it's rare." Then, they say "OK, it's happening frequently, but that's a good thing!" We're getting closer and closer to that third one. I suppose what's "rare" and what isn't is open to interpretation. But there's no denying that trans athletes are upstaging females often enough for anyone paying attention to notice. articles.title: Aces star A'ja Wilson gets into heated exchange with fan in Game 2 loss to Fever: 'That is unacceptable'
articles.summary: A'ja Wilson was livid and had to be held back from the fan sitting underneath the basket at Gainbridge Fieldhouse.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson got into it with a fan sitting at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Tuesday late in their Game 2 loss to the Indiana Fever .

And she did not hold back on the man after the game, either.

"I've never seen A'ja Wilson go like that," Aces head coach Becky Hammon said after their 99-89 loss. "So whatever was done, I can tell you she felt very disrespected in that moment. I've never seen her really react like that, ever."

Wilson was trying to fight through a screen set by Sophie Cunningham midway through the fourth quarter in Indianapolis when the two got tangled up. Cunningham was sent down to the court hard, and was called for a foul.

But as Wilson was walking down the lane after play had stopped, she suddenly erupted at a fan sitting behind the basket. Wilson had to be pulled back by several teammates and officials. It's unclear what was actually said by the fan to spark the exchange, but Wilson was livid.

The fan was removed from his seat briefly, but returned soon after and was spotted celebrating with people sitting around him, according to Fever reporter Tony East .

"If I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don't give a damn what you said. I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable," Wilson said after the game. "You don't know me to step toward me and point at me. I'm not for that s*** at all … That there is unacceptable. How he gets back in the game because they said he didn't do anything, of course he did."

After a lengthy review, Wilson was assessed a technical foul and Cunningham was called for a personal foul. Kelsey Mitchell missed the free throw for the Fever, while Wilson hit both of hers. That made it a nine-point game with 4:10 left in the contest.

Wilson said that she apologized to her team for the technical foul, but she's not sorry for her actions.

"It's just certain things that I'm not going to allow anymore, because it's unacceptable," she said. "You don't know me at all to come and step toward me and point at me and say anything."

The Fever released a statement on the incident after the game, saying they are not going to investigate the matter further. The fan in question, they said, did not violate their rules and was allowed to return.

"Following a report of a comment directed toward a player, arena security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses," the team said, via The Athletic's James Boyd . "Security determined there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct, the fan was not removed from the arena. We consider the matter closed."

After the chaos, the Fever held on down the stretch to grab the 10-point win . That tied the series up and forced a deciding Game 3 on Thursday night in Las Vegas . The winner will advance into the semifinals.

Caitlin Clark had 27 points and 15 assists to lead the Fever while shooting 9-of-18 from the field. Kelsey Mitchell added 26 points, and Aliyah Boston finished with 22 points. Jackie Young led the Aces with 31 points in the loss, and Wilson finished with 22 points and nine rebounds.

Wilson averaged 26.2 points and 9.4 rebounds per game this season, her ninth in the league. The four-time MVP, who has won the award in back-to-back seasons now, is widely considered the favorite to win the award again this season.

While things got heated in Indianapolis, Wilson will have a much friendlier crowd for the winner-take-all Game 3 on Thursday. A fan interaction like she had on Tuesday shouldn't be something she has to worry about.

"You don't have to like me, you don't have to love me," she said. "You can hate me with all your heart. But you don't know me. "But I guarantee you will respect me."

"You don't have to like me, you don't have to love me," she said. "You can hate me with all your heart. But you don't know me.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's historic double-double helps Fever force Game 3 with win over Aces
articles.summary: A trip to the semifinals will be on the line in Las Vegas on Thursday night.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever picked up a 99-89 win over the Las Vegas Aces on Tuesday night to force Game 3 of their WNBA first-round playoff series, and Caitlin Clark made history in the process.

Indiana was led by Clark, Aliyah Boston , and Kelsey Mitchell , who all finished with more than 20 points each and combined for 75 points as a trio. They combined for only 45 in Game 1.

Clark had a double-double in the first half with 14 points and 11 assists, marking the first time in WNBA history that a player had a points-assists double-double in the first half of a playoff game.

Las Vegas won the first game of the series in dominant fashion, but had no answer for Indiana's paint presence in Game 2. Fifty-eight of the Fever 's total points came from inside the paint, compared to 26 for the Aces.

In the Game 1 loss, Indiana still had more paint points than Las Vegas, 36-34, but it was a combination of paint offense and paint defense that helped spur the Game 2 victory to even the series.

Part of the paint dominance came from second-chance points. The Fever had 11 offensive rebounds, helping keep possessions alive. Alternatively, the Aces had only seven offensive boards.

Las Vegas took an early first-quarter lead, but Indiana immediately fought back. The Fever outscored the Aces 30-17 in the second quarter and 24-17 in the third quarter, building a cushion. The early effort helped give Indiana some wiggle room as Las Vegas tried to claw its way back.

It didn't help that the Fever had to finish the game without their star guard. Clark fouled out with 2:45 left in the game while guarding A'ja Wilson in the paint. The Aces used that momentum shift to pull within five, but it was too little, too late for a possible comeback.

The winner-take-all series finale will be held on Thursday back in Las Vegas.

Clark appeared to disagree with the officiating throughout much of the first half. It didn't feel consistent, but the Fever star let her emotions get the best of her. She was having a rough half, with five early turnovers, but then got whistled for a foul she took exception to.

The Indiana guard jawed and waved her arms toward the officials, which got the foul upgraded to a technical.

After that, Clark was locked in. She shot better from the field and didn't commit a single turnover in the second half.

But she continued to pick up fouls and earned her sixth with 2:45 left. Had the Aces pulled off the comeback, that would have been a huge factor, but with the win, Clark and her teammates will turn their attention to using this momentum heading into Thursday's series finale.

Wilson, who finished with 22 points, 9 rebounds and 2 blocks, was fouled by Sophie Cunningham in the fourth quarter. Afterward, the Aces star was walking down the lane toward the baseline and a fan in the crowd grabbed her attention. Wilson was incensed by whatever the fan did or said and stepped into the crowd , pointing and yelling.

When the dust settled, the fan was removed, and Wilson was assessed a technical foul. Later the fan returned to his seat and was reportedly met with applause from those around him.

After the game, Wilson addressed the situation.

"If I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don't give a damn what you said. I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable," Wilson said after the game. "You don't know me to step toward me and point at me. I'm not for that s*** at all … That there is unacceptable. How he gets back in the game because they said he didn't do anything, of course he did."

The Fever released a statement on the fan interaction: "Following a report of a comment directed toward a player, arena security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses. Security determined there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct, the fan was not removed from the arena. We consider the matter closed."

articles.title: Josh Hart Reveals Surgery That Would End NBA Career Amid Finger Injury Ahead of Knicks Season
articles.summary: New York Knicks guard Josh Hart is going to continue playing with his finger wrapped.
articles.body:
New York Knicks guard Josh Hart is going to continue playing with his finger wrapped.

Because his only other option is having a career-ending surgery.

Hart took to social media Tuesday and responded to an image of him practicing with his finger taped by revealing the only surgery that would fix his injury would be a joint replacement that ended his career:

What NBA's Vegas expansion team is going to cost

"So it will be wrapped until I retire," he said.

The wrap didn't appear to limit him last season, as he connected on 41.3 percent of his three-point attempts while averaging 12 points per game. It was a drastic improvement from the 2024-25 campaign when he hit 33.3 percent of his triples.

Hart did far more than just hit three-pointers, though, as he was the role player who did a little bit of everything for the Knicks on the way to the championship.

He also averaged 7.4 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.1 steals per game while assuming more of the defensive responsibilities so Jalen Brunson could lead the way on the offensive side.

And Hart will forever be a Knicks legend as a key part of the team that won the franchise's first championship since 1973. He scored in double figures in two of the last three NBA Finals games against the San Antonio Spurs and also exploded for 26 points in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

If the Knicks are going to defend their crown, they will need Hart on the floor and impacting the game in a number of ways just like he did last season.

So he will not undergo the joint replacement surgery that would have otherwise ended his career.

articles.title: Una camiseta de Michael Jordan se vende por 12,26 millones: The Last Dance de las Finales NBA de 1998
articles.standfirst: Auperan el anterior récord de la NBA, 10,1 millones de dólares para otra camiseta llevada por Jordan en esas Finales.
articles.summary: Auperan el anterior récord de la NBA, 10,1 millones de dólares para otra camiseta llevada por Jordan en esas Finales.
articles.body: Una camiseta de Michael Jordan usada en las Finales NBA de 1998 ganadas por los Chicago Bulls a los Utah Jazz se vendió por la cifra de 12,26 millones de dólares, un récord para una camiseta de colección de la liga de baloncesto estadounidense. La camiseta salió a subasta el pasado 15 de septiembre en la plataforma de comercio Joopiter, fundada por el artista Pharrell Williams, y un coleccionista se la adjudicó este martes. Los 12,26 millones de dólares pagados por esta camiseta superan el anterior récord de la NBA, 10,1 millones de dólares para otra elástica llevada por Jordan en esas Finales. "Usada durante 'The Last Dance' - la última temporada en la que el mejor jugador de baloncesto de todos los tiempos ganó un campeonato -, marca la culminación de una era que transformó el baloncesto en un fenómeno cultural global", destacó la plataforma. El '23' fue el máximo anotador esa noche con 24 puntos que contribuyeron a que los Bulls se llevaran la victoria y se adelantaran 2-1 en la serie. Esa eliminatoria fue la sexta y última aparición de Jordan en unas finales de la NBA, y concluyó con su sexto anillo gracias a una de sus jugadas más emblemáticas: 'The Last Shot', en la que puso por delante a los Bulls con un tiro de dos puntos a falta de 5 segundos. Joopiter sacó a subasta el pasado diciembre las icónicas zapatillas Nike Kobe 6 'Grinch', que empleó Kobe Bryant en el partido de Navidad de 2010 contra los Miami Heat de LeBron James, también por un precio mínimo de 10 millones de dólares. Además, un cromo firmado por Bryant y Jordan fue subastado el pasado agosto por más de 12,9 millones de dólares (unos 11 millones de euros) por la casa de subastas Heritage Auctions, una cantidad récord para una tarjeta de este tipo en Estados Unidos y que lo convirtió en el segundo objeto de coleccionismo deportivo más caro de todos los tiempos.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Reveals Fever's Mindset in Win vs. Aces to Avoid Elimination in 2026 WNBA Playoffs
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever saved their season on Tuesday night, beating the Las Vegas Aces 99-89 and set up a decisive Game 3 on Thursday.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever saved their season on Tuesday night, beating the Las Vegas Aces 99-89 and set up a decisive Game 3 on Thursday.

"The way I looked at it, your back's up against the wall," Clark told reporters after the win. "This is the only opportunity you're guaranteed to have is these 40 minutes, and you know you're going to go down swinging if you're going to lose. But I think we had the mentality like this was one we were going to win, no matter what and do it for our fans."

Clark was brilliant in the contest, putting up 27 points and 15 assists. She was so good that she already had a double-double by halftime, making her the first player in WNBA playoff history to have a points-assist double-double in the first half.

"I thought her energy from start to finish—I mean a double-double in the first half—was pretty incredible," Fever head coach Stephanie White told reporters. "The way she moved the ball, attacked from multiple positions. ... You always expect to be able to make shots and facilitate. But I thought how she managed the game was really good and her defensive energy I thought was terrific. It's what we need from her."

articles.title: Olivia Miles, Lynx on Wrong Side of History with 2026 WNBA Playoff Elimination to 8th Seed Liberty
articles.summary: The Minnesota Lynx made the kind of history no team wants to make Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Lynx made the kind of history no team wants to make Tuesday.

While Minnesota finished with the best record in the WNBA during the regular season, its postseason came to a swift end with an 87-71 loss to the New York Liberty. New York completed the brief two-game sweep and ensured the Lynx were the first No. 1 seed to lose to a No. 8 seed in league history.

Olivia Miles was brilliant for much of the season but struggled with five points on 1-of-8 shooting from the field after she was just 3-of-12 shooting in the Game 1 loss. Napheesa Collier was just 6-of-14 from the field, as the one-two punch of stars was unable to counter New York's dominant trio.

Jonquel Jones was unstoppable down low with a double-double of 21 points and 13 rebounds, while Sabrina Ionescu added 18 points and seven assists. Breanna Stewart also did a little bit of everything with 21 points, five rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks.

Those names alone underscore the reality the Liberty are not a typical No. 8 seed.

While the regular season was a roller coaster of inconsistency with injuries and poor play at times, that is still a group of champions who can each take over any game at any time.

Minnesota learned that the hard way with a quick two-game sweep, but the rest of the teams in the playoffs surely took note as well. The Liberty aren't far removed from their 2024 title and have the same group of stars leading the way this time around.

They already made history Tuesday and will now turn their focus toward once again reaching the WNBA mountaintop.

articles.title: Liberty roll over Lynx again to complete historic WNBA playoff upset, reach semifinals
articles.summary: The Liberty are now the first No. 8 seed to knock off a No. 1 seed in the WNBA playoffs.
articles.body: After dominating the league throughout the regular season, the Minnesota Lynx are done. The New York Liberty picked up a second straight runaway win over the Lynx, this time a 87-71 victory at the Barclays Center on Tuesday night, to officially close out their opening-round playoff series. That knocked the top seed out of the postseason and made the Liberty the first No. 8 seed to upset a No. 1 seed in WNBA playoff history. The current playoff format, with all eight teams playing in the opening round, was only adopted in 2022. But the Liberty were the first No. 8 seed to even win a game in the opening round of the playoffs, and no No. 8 team has ever won an opening-round series, even before they were going up against the top seed.The Lynx entered the postseason as the top seed with both Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles and Coach of the Year Cheryl Reeve on their side. They went 33-10 on the season, and seemed poised to go on a meaningful playoff run. But the Liberty went into the Target Center on Sunday with other plans. Breanna Stewart dropped 34 points in that contest to lead them to a convincing 16-point road win. Tuesday night was no different. The Liberty led from the jump at home, and opened the contest on a 15-5 run before taking a 14-point lead at halftime. Though the Lynx responded briefly in the third quarter — they went on a brief 10-2 run to cut the deficit to single digits — Sabrina Ionescu drilled a huge 3-pointer just before the end of the period to give them control.JUST BEFORE THE 3RD ENDED.Sabrina Ionescu. That's it. That's the tweet. 😮‍💨16 PTS | 5 AST | 4 REB | 4 3PM pic.twitter.com/AL0H2yV7S7— WNBA (@WNBA) September 30, 2026 The Liberty answered every time, and ended up cruising the rest of the way to the 16-point win. The Lynx, unlike how they looked throughout the regular season, were no match. Minnesota led for only three minutes, 23 seconds over the two games in this series.Courtney Williams led the Lynx with 18 points and seven rebounds in the loss. Both Napheesa Collier and Kayla McBride added 14 points each. Jonquel Jones led the Liberty with 21 points, 14 of which came in the first half, and 13 rebounds in the win. Stewart had 21 points, and Ionescu added 18 points and seven assists.The Liberty now advance to the semifinals. They'll take on either the Atlanta Dream or Washington Mystics in the next round in a best-of-five series. If they can pull off a series win there, they'll earn a third trip to the WNBA Finals in the past four seasons. The Lynx, though, are headed home. After the season they had, this early playoff exit can't be seen as anything other than disappointing.

articles.title: Michael Jordan 'Last Dance' Game-Worn Jersey Becomes Most Expensive in NBA History with Record Sale
articles.summary: Michael Jordan is still setting records 28 years after his "Last Dance" season with the Chicago Bulls.
articles.body:
Michael Jordan is still setting records 28 years after his "Last Dance" season with the Chicago Bulls.

Well, memorabilia tied to His Airness is at least.

Kurt Badenhausen of Sportico reported Jordan's Game 3 jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals victory over the Utah Jazz sold for a record $12.3 million through the auction platform Joopiter, which was founded by musician Pharrell Williams.

What NBA's Vegas expansion team is going to cost

The previous record sale price for an NBA jersey was Jordan's Game 1 jersey from that same series, which sold for $10.1 million in 2022.

Still, both numbers are well behind the highest price for any sports jersey, which was Babe Ruth's "called shot" one from the 1932 World Series that sold for a stunning $24.1 million in 2024.

"I've always felt like when I own these things, I'm a steward of a piece of history," Rob Gough, who was the seller, said of the latest Jordan jersey to sell at a record price.

Chicago cruised to a 96-54 victory in Game 3 of the 1998 NBA Finals in a contest that stood out from the rest of the series. The other five games were decided by five points or less, including the decisive Game 6 when Jordan hit the winning shot in a one-point victory.

The Hall of Famer played just 32 minutes in the Game 3 blowout and finished with a game-high 24 points.

The series was Jordan's final one with the Bulls, and he fittingly played the role of hero in Game 6 with a late steal and jumper to secure his sixth championship. It was the third straight title in his second threepeat with the first coming from 1991-93.

And now one of the jerseys he wore during that series sold for more than $12 million.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark keeps Fever's season alive with fiery, historic performance in Game 2 vs. Aces: 'She was the catalyst'
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark said the Fever's mantra in Game 2 was "don't be soft." Mission accomplished.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — The scenes 48 hours and 1,849 miles apart were stark. In the first, a morose Caitlin Clark covered her face with a towel draped over her head, her words sharp and direct in attacking a performance her head coach said humbled them . Two days later, Clark beams amid the bright Gainbridge Fieldhouse lights once more, interjecting when someone mentions her fiery competitiveness.

"You think?" she laughs, eyes alight, praise and talking points ready after a 99-89 win over the Las Vegas Aces in Game 2 of the WNBA playoffs first round on Tuesday night.

Clark will not say how ticked off she was by a Game 1 blowout that put the backs of the championship-aspiring Indiana Fever to the wall. What she will do is point out that she hit three shots in a row after the officiating crew called her for a technical foul less than two minutes into the second quarter.

On a night she said the referees struggled — a claim neither side of the court disagreed with — she said she respected the referees for calling it.

Yes, she said, she definitely deserved it. No, she answers, she didn't do it on purpose. No doubt, though, that it further lit a necessary fire.

"We didn't have the mentality [in Game 1] of coming in, kind of puffing our chests a little bit, and I think tonight we really had that," Clark said after sticking hers out with 27 points, 15 assists and 7 rebounds.

The MVP candidate credited Myisha Hines-Allen for the pregame prompting. In the later minutes of the first quarter, Hines-Allen dusted up with Aces center and Game 1 superstar A'ja Wilson, to which Sophie Cunningham waved her hands up to hear from a raucous home crowd, and Clark slapped her singular championship-winning vet's hands.

"That's what we talked about as a team is like, don't be soft," Clark said. "We kind of beat ourselves in that way."

A minute later, Clark reached in on Wilson and ripped the ball to force a jump ball. With every centimeter of movement, the series wrested from the grasp of Wilson to that of Clark. Now it goes back to Las Vegas tied 1-1, and everyone's season is on the line.

"It's about getting hit, but understanding like, listen, we gotta get back up," Aliyah Boston told Yahoo Sports. "You cannot just lay there."

They called it a bounce-back. The intentionality was as clear as the mood shift. In the locker room, head coach Stephanie White drew up the first play to key open Clark on the perimeter. White told everyone she was going to make it.

"I was just trying not to let everybody down because we were all visualizing that I was going to make it, so I needed to get the night started off right," Clark said.

It officially clocked in at 29 feet, a mere 15 seconds into the contest. An early trademark 3 portends a good night for Clark, and Game 2 didn't disappoint. She drew contact for another three points at the free-throw line, thought an ensuing 27-footer would fall ("it just rolled out," she noted), and used the attention to feed Makayla Timpson and Boston on cuts inside an open paint.

Boston finished through contact around Wilson, nearly pristine in her attack and movements, for 22 points on 15 attempts. Kelsey Mitchell did her work as usual, scoring 26 with a sharp 3 of 4 line from the perimeter. Everyone who played scored. They shot a combined 52.1%.

"We just had a presence about us right from the start of the game," Clark said.

Though the Fever looked to be back in business, the deficit grew to eight by the first quarter's end. Jewell Loyd 's 3-pointer to open the second frame sent it to 11.

The Aces, who have only lost a series to the New York Liberty in the playoffs over the last four years, ran over the Fever in Game 1 with a proper sense of understood urgency and desperation. They knew what to expect, knew how to handle it, and operated accordingly.

White described her team as young in that area before the series began, and they swiftly proved the point. An unraveling began in the second quarter the first time around. When the initial thread began to come apart this time, they didn't let it snowball.

Composure, Boston said, was paramount. Except, well, you know.

"She's just a passionate player," Boston said, laughing at hearing that White and the coaching staff's focus was keeping Clark calm following the technical.

The whistle of Clark's first postseason tech blew in a nine-point deficit. She knows how many consecutive baskets she hit afterward: three. Not including a missed 3-pointer. Also not included: a feed to Boston in the paint, where they tore through the Aces in the first half to a tune of 30-16.

Another 3 drew the Fever within a possession, eliciting a roar from the crowd and a timeout by the Aces. They fell behind by six when Mitchell, the league's second-highest scorer, took a turn. Her running alley-oop off an Aces turnover and Clark assist gave the Fever a lead.

Clark became the first player in postseason history with at least 10 points and 10 assists in a half, setting the mark for most assists with 11. She had 14 points when the Fever led 48-43 at the half. Combined with Mitchell's 12 and Boston's eight, their big three contributed 70% of the scoring. The Aces' trio of A'ja Wilson (10 points), Chelsea Gray (10) and Jackie Young (7) had 27 of 43 in the first half.

"I mean, a double-double in the first half? Pretty incredible," White said. "The way that she moved the ball and attacked from multiple positions. You always expect her to be able to make shots and to facilitate, but I thought how she managed the game was really good and her defensive energy, I thought, was terrific."

The Fever leveled up the Aces in the physicality department, suffocating Wilson into attempting zero field goals in the third quarter. She finished with 22 points, largely rendered ineffective. Jackie Young brought the Aces back into it with a 31-point performance that wasn't enough to make up for 10 points by Gray, and single digits elsewhere.

Clark, meanwhile, shone — though the drawback of such fiery, un-soft approach did rear its head. She fouled out with 2:45 to go when she stepped into the block, attempting to stop a solo Wilson from an easy bucket.

The Fever challenged to no avail. A nervousness settled around the crowd, unsure if losing their attack-mode superstar would unspool a 92-83 lead. Mitchell lay in her trademark finger-roll, Boston drove in. Lexie Hull rebounded two key Aces misses, and Cunningham hit two free throws.

Clark said she intends to "keep my head a little bit more" in the next game, aware that one point could be the difference. The Fever need her on the floor, and at her best.

"She was the catalyst for us here tonight," White said. "And I think she's going to just take it to another level when we go to Game 3."

The fire has to travel. Or else the scene reverses itself again.
