articles.title: ‘He Was Horrible’ — JJ Redick Gets Brutally Honest About Former Lakers Guard
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers, along with the rest of the NBA, are more than ready to kick off the 2026-27 season in October. Of course, the Lakers and head coach J...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers , along with the rest of the NBA, are more than ready to kick off the 2026-27 season in October. Of course, the Lakers and head coach JJ Redick have some bigger fish to fry — make the playoffs and win without LeBron James on the team.

And while LA has Luka Dončić to rely on, Redick also has to manage the rest of their roster. This includes players competing for spots and multiple training sessions, which require the coach to be honest about what's needed for their franchise.

Lakers HC JJ Redick Gets Candid About 'Horrible' Former Guard

In a recent media interaction before the NBA preseason kicks off, Redick was asked about competition for spots during training camps and the effort required to balance the roster so the team stays together.

The reporter also mentioned Redick's stint as an NBA player, which offered a different perspective on the matter. And while Redick didn't deny the competitive spirit, he didn't think the system was about balancing things.

"I don't think that there's finding a balance," Redick told the reporter. "I think it's about creating competition. Recognizing that every guy is going to have an opportunity throughout the season. That's just the reality of the NBA now."

Getting specific about his explanation, Redick zeroed in on Max Christie , a former Lakers guard currently with the Dallas Mavericks .

"Max Christie, our first year, was in the rotation," Redick said. "He was horrible to start the year. We told him that he wasn't doing what we asked him to do. He didn't play."

Redick explained that it was only when Christie put in the work that he started earning his minutes. "And then, when he got back into the rotation, he eventually earned a starting spot and he turned our season around."

The Lakers' head coach doubled down on his initial statement, adding that the league is competitive by nature. "This is a meritocracy. If anybody tells you otherwise, it's [expletive]."

Currently with the Mavericks, Christie was a second-round pick by the Lakers. Eventually becoming a reliable role player for the team, he was traded to the Mavericks during the league-altering Dončić trade in 2025.

During media day , the 23-year-old admitted he is excited about a growing role in Dallas, adding that he has been working on his skills and hopes to stay in his best shape this season.

That being said, Lake Show Life's Svyatoslav Rovenchuk hinted at the possibility of the Lakers reuniting with Christie.

"Meanwhile, over in Dallas, Christie could enter unrestricted free agency next summer," Rovenchuk wrote . "All that he would need to do is decline his $8.9 million player option for 2027-28. Austin Reaves gave back money on his new extension. Sandro Mamukelashvili took a second-year dip on his new deal. That should give the Lakers access to the money necessary to pursue a reunion in free agency."

The Mavericks, however, might not be willing to let a young player walk away — especially as they could build a core team around Cooper Flagg .

The Lakers will start their campaign with a preseason clash with the Sacramento Kings on Monday, October 5. The Mavericks will begin their preseason with a game against the Houston Rockets on October 9 in China.

The Lakers and Mavericks will face each other during the regular season on Sunday, February 28, at the American Airlines Center in Dallas.

articles.title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry Makes Announcement Before New Season
articles.summary: Veteran Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry made an announcement on Tuesday regarding his media company, Unanimous Media. The post Warriors’ Stephen Cu...
articles.body:
Veteran Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry made an announcement on Tuesday regarding his media company, Unanimous Media.

The two-time MVP revealed details of a new subscription-based service that will give fans in-depth access to "Sincer3ly," a Substack covering stories from him and his colleagues at Unanimous Media.

"We've got a lot cooking with Sincer3ly," wrote the iconic sharpshooter.

"MVP gets you a little closer to the action with exclusive content, early access, more from me and the @Unanimous_World family, and some surprises along the way.

"Think of it as a spot in the starting 5," he added.

Curry further informed that every subscription will give back to classrooms across the Untied States through the Donors Choose organization.

Curry made the announcement a day after attending his 18th Media Day in the NBA . It was his first public appearance after he inked a two-year, $116M extension to remain with the Warriors through the 2028-29 season.

In the lead up to his extension, some analysts and fans urged Curry to take his talents to a legitimate title contender to pursue his fifth NBA title. However, the 38-year-old made it clear on Monday that he had no intention to leave the Bay Area franchise.

"This is home, this is what we've built, this is the community that I've played in front of my entire career and being able to finish the story the right way is a big part of, I think, what I control, thankfully, hopefully health-wise as well," Curry told reporters.

"I know the list, a short list of guys that have been able to do it, but reimagining what that looks like with the level that I feel like I can play at down the stretch of my career.

"There's a pride of representing the Bay, representing this franchise, that when I stepped foot here in '09 and what we've all been able to accomplish, this isn't just a 'me' thing, it's a 'we.' I want to do right by that."

Curry was referring to the likes of Kobe Bryant , Tim Duncan and Magic Johnson, who spent their entire careers with one franchise and captured five NBA titles apiece.

Per multiple reports, Curry left nearly $20M on the table to allow the Warriors to build a title contender. As a result of his sacrifice, the Warriors could reportedly have up to $64M in cap space next summer, when the likes of Nikola Jokic , Giannis Antetokounmpo and Karl-Anthony Towns could become free agents.

"Yes, I was presented the max. Yes, there was everything on the table," he said.

"It was a very, kind of, thoughtful journey, partnership of putting all the different scenarios out there. It was of interest of making sure I was here, figuring out what was in the best setup for me, for the team, for the now, for the flexibility the rest of my career.

"So trying to balance all of that is such a unique situation with all of the circumstances of where we've been the last four years, what's currently on the table and where we're trying to go to be competitive and give ourselves a chance."

articles.title: Cameron Boozer Earns Praise From Teammate
articles.summary: Former Duke Basketball star Cameron Boozer has earned some praise from another teammate ahead of the season.
articles.body:
Basketball season is right around the corner, and it will be on our TV's before we know at both the pro and college levels. While Duke has opened up practices already for the 2026-27 season, the NBA will be underway soon as well.

Teams hosted media days this past week and it gave fans a chance to see the roster for the first time ahead of the preseason. It also gives players a chance to meet the media and discuss the offseason as well as what they expect for the upcoming season.

In Memphis, the story is former Duke star Cameron Boozer .

The rookie was selected No. 3 overall in the 2026 NBA Draft by the Memphis Grizzlies back in June. They hope that Boozer can be a star player for the franchise, especially after they made moves this offseason including trading Ja Morant. The Boozer era will officially begin in a few weeks when the regular season tips off.

Before then, he's earned some praise from national analysts, former teammates and current teammates.

The latest is former Virginia guard Ty Jerome who spoke highly of Boozer at media day this week. Jerome has been in the league for a few years now, so he's played with a lot of different players. His praise for Boozer was not only his skill-set but his mindset as well.

Jerome says he believes Boozer has to be one of the most mature 19-year-olds he's seen so far. He points to both on and off the court and says he has a great feel for the game already.

Duke fans saw that maturity for one season with the Blue Devils. Boozer arrived as a five-star recruit, and early on, he became a leader for that team. The forward showcased what he can do not only on the floor but off the floor as well.

Boozer will have pressure on him to deliver early in his rookie year. The expectations are high for him and Memphis hopes he can prove them right early. With this being such a loaded draft class, Boozer could end up being the best player among the prospects.

Last season, Memphis won just 25 games and it forced them to make some big moves in the offseason. That was headlined by trading Morant and trying to build around a young core again that is centered on Boozer, among others.

articles.title: La NBA se acerca a acuerdos con grandes clubes europeos de fútbol para crear la NBA Europa
articles.standfirst: "La NBA busca atraer el gran poder económico y la fortaleza de marca de algunos de los principales clubes de fútbol europeos como miembros fundadores de NBA Europa"
articles.summary: "La NBA busca atraer el gran poder económico y la fortaleza de marca de algunos de los principales clubes de fútbol europeos como miembros fundadores de NBA Europa"
articles.body: El 'New York Times' publica que "la NBA avanza hacia acuerdos con varios clubes de fútbol europeos de gran prestigio para ayudar a poner en marcha una nueva liga continental de baloncesto en Europa". Joe Vardon y Matt Slater informan cuatro fuentes con conocimiento directo de las negociaciones les confirmaron esta información a 'The Athletic'. "Desde hace tiempo, la NBA busca atraer el gran poder económico y la fortaleza de marca de algunos de los principales clubes de fútbol europeos para que actúen como miembros fundadores de NBA Europe, proyecto cuyo lanzamiento está previsto para el próximo otoño", apuntan. Mark Tatum, subcomisionado de la NBA y principal representante del comisionado Adam Silver en asuntos internacionales, asistió como invitado a la conferencia anual de clubes de fútbol europeos, organizada por la EFC y por Nasser Al-Khelaifi, presidente del Paris Saint-Germain. "Obviamente, no habrían invitado a Tatum si las cosas con los clubes de fútbol no avanzaran en la dirección correcta", comentó un representante de un importante club de fútbol interesado durante la conferencia de Copenhague. NBA Europa tiene previsto comenzar con 12 equipos fundadores y cuatro plazas adicionales. Esas 12 sedes principales se ubicarán en Londres, París, Roma, Milán, Berlín, Múnich, Estambul, Madrid, Atenas, Barcelona, Mánchester y Lyon. "Hemos aprendido muchísimo del fútbol europeo a lo largo de los años. Lanzamos un torneo durante la temporada, la NBA Cup. Esa idea se tomó directamente del fútbol y del deporte europeos, donde existen estos torneos de copa dentro de las temporadas; nos preguntamos: "¿Por qué no podemos hacer lo mismo?". Así que aplicamos ese modelo a nuestra liga. Creo que uno de los objetivos que perseguimos con nuestra iniciativa en Europa —como ya he mencionado— es replicar algunas de las grandes lecciones derivadas de lo que ustedes han construido aquí. El fútbol es, sin duda, el deporte más importante del mundo. El fútbol europeo constituye una de las mayores entidades comerciales a nivel global, y nosotros simplemente intentamos aprender todo lo posible de las personas presentes en esta sala", explicó Tatum. Tatum, que abogó por la construcción de nuevos pabellones en Europa, citó la incorporación de publicidad en las camisetas de los equipos de la NBA como otro concepto que la liga estadounidense de baloncesto tomó prestado del fútbol europeo: "Si el Manchester United puede retirar su nombre de la camiseta para colocar el de un patrocinador, sin duda los Chicago Bulls pueden incluir un pequeño parche en la suya. Nosotros utilizamos ese ejemplo para vender la idea a los propietarios de los equipos de la NBA (hace nueve años)".

articles.summary: Primera jugadora en la historia de la WNBA en lograr al menos 25 puntos y 15 asistencias en un partido
articles.body: Caitlin Clark firmó 27 puntos, 7 rebotes y 15 asistencias (primera jugadora en la historia de la WNBA en lograr al menos 25 puntos y 15 asistencias en un partido) para entregar a las Indiana Fever un trascendental 99-89 en casa contra Las Vegas Aces, lo que ha forzado un tercer y decisivo partido de la serie de primera ronda de los 'playoffs' de la WNBA. Clark acabó expulsada por faltas a tres minutos para el final del cuarto período, pero sus Fever, que estaban arriba 92-83 en ese momento, consiguieron tumbar a las vigentes campeonas para asegurar un tercer partido, en Las Vegas, el jueves 1 de octubre. Antes, Clark hizo historia con una primera mitad en la que llevaba un doble doble de 14 puntos y 11 asistencias, una marca nunca vista en los 'playoffs' de la WNBA. La ex de Iowa contó con el apoyo de una Kelsey Mitchell de 26 puntos, mientras Aliyah Boston aportó 22. Para las Aces, la cuádruple MVP A'ja Wilson metió 22 puntos y 9 rebotes. A'ja Wilson explicó su enfrentamiento en los Playoffs de la WNBA con un aficionado de las Indiana Fever, que avanzó hacia ella mientras la señalaba con el dedo. La estrella de Las Vegas Aces, que saltó tras tener un rifirrafe con Sophie Cunningham por el que fue sancionada con técnica, calificó dicha conducta de inaceptable. Sin embargo, la versión de Indiana ofreció una valoración distinta, al afirmar que el personal de seguridad del estadio no detectó ninguna infracción del Código de Conducta para Aficionados y, por tanto, no expulsó al espectador. "Si veo que un hombre se me echa encima, dando pasos hacia mí y señalándome... me importa un bledo lo que hayas dicho... articles.title: Satoransky explica por qué dejó el Barcelona y ratifica su ataque a sus dirigentes: "Lo pasé mal al final"
articles.standfirst: El ex capitán del FC Barcelona afronta un nuevo reto en el Hapoel Tel Aviv
articles.summary: El ex capitán del FC Barcelona afronta un nuevo reto en el Hapoel Tel Aviv
articles.body: El base checo, Tomas Satoransky, acaba de firmar por el Hapoel de Tel Aviv tras finalizar su contrato con el FC Barcelona. El de Praga se pasó por los micrófonos de 'Nos Gusta el Basket' para repasar sus primeras sensaciones con el equipo israelí, los objetivos del curso y su etapa como capitán azulgrana. "Fue una decisión también familiar, sabía que no iba a continuar en Barcelona y queríamos probar alguna cosa diferente, obviamente mantenerme en Euroliga. Lo que me convenció fue la llamada del entrenador explicándome lo que esperaba de mí. Fue un factor muy importante en la decisión. No fue fácil, pero tampoco tenía mucho tiempo. Sabíamos que la situación sería complicada porque es un año de viajar mucho y por eso hemos decidido que será un año", explicó sobre su fichaje por el conjunto que entrena Dimitris Itoudis Satoransky pasará de ser el base titular del FC Barcelona y acumular minutos y kilómetros en las últimas temporadas a cambiar su rol para acompañar en el dirección del Hapoel al serbio Vassilje Micic. "Es un poco natural y algo que quiero porque me estaba quejando un poco de los minutos y el rol de los últimos años con dos competiciones tan exigentes. Estaba buscando algo un rol así, en el que no se espera tanto protagonismo de mí, pero en el que puedo ayudar en cualquier cosa", apuntó. El Hapoel, que volverá a jugar sus encuentros como local en Sofía, la capital de Bulgaria, aspira a pelear de nuevo por jugar la Final Four. La temporada pasada lideraron la Euroliga durante varias jornadas y cayeron en el Playoff ante el Real Madrid. "Es un poco peligroso hablar de objetivos antes de empezar la temporada. La Euroliga está súper igualada, realmente el objetivo tendría que ser jugar la Final Four porque el año pasado ya estuvieron varios meses primeros, se metieron en el Playoff y ahora quieres hacer un poco más. El baloncesto Euroliga atrae a los jugadores americanos, cada vez vienen más a jugar a Europa. Creo que el nivel se está acercando con la NBA". Precisamente, el Real Madrid de Pedro Martínez asoma en el horizonte como uno de los primeros rivales europeos del nuevo curso. "Pedro Martínez ha trabajado muy bien su estilo para transmitirlo en el Real Madrid. Obviamente, algunas cosas no puedes hacerla como en Valencia, pero tienen un juego atractivo, rápido, con muchos tiros...y no hay que olvidar que ellos tienen la identidad del Real Madrid y pelean por todos los títulos", comentó. Los últimos años no están siendo fáciles para el baloncesto azulgrana, desde la salida de Jasikevicius, el Barcelona no ha conseguido levantar ningún título en las últimas temporadas, una situación difícil que el checo ha vivido muy de cerca como capitán. "No lo he pasado mal, el Barça es el club de mi vida. Hemos estado 6 años allí y hemos estado muy bien. En una entrevista en mi país dije que sentía que los de arriba no querían que ganáramos y yo no cambiaría mis palabras. Creo que otra de las razones es que no podíamos hacer más y obviamente mucha culpa la tenemos los jugadores por los rendimientos, pero a lo mejor me dolía más por ser culé. Creo que han hecho un equipo interesante, querían cambiar todo y lo que he visto me ha gustado. Espero que lo pasen bien y les deseo todo lo mejor. Lo he pasado mal al final porque no hemos tenido éxito". En el FC Barcelona compartió vestuario con dos de los protagonistas del arranque del curso baloncestístico como Nico Laprovittola y Willy Hernangómez. "Me alegro mucho por Lapro, se veía que tenía hambre, energía y ambición de enseñar otra vez que todavía puede jugar al nivel que todos conocemos de él. Willy también está pasando una situación nueva, tiene que demostrar que vale como jugador. Creo que el Unicaja y su entrenador le puede venir muy bien", explicó. El base checo conoce a la perfección también el baloncesto americano por su paso por la NBA y se mostró favorable a una posible unión entre dos gigantes del baloncesto mundial. "Es importante que si se juntan estas dos competiciones que lleguen a un acuerdo en común para que no dañe el baloncesto en Europa. Los americanos pueden atraer gente, dinero, negocio, ven que hay mucho potencial en este producto. Sería muy interesante traer más equipos y ciudades, pero se tiene que trabajar colectivamente", finalizó.

articles.title: Who is LaMelo Ball’s baby mama? Meet Ana Montana who is facing felony drug charges in North Carolina
articles.summary: Ana Montana, the model and social media influencer linked to NBA star LaMelo Ball, is facing felony drug charges in North Carolina.
articles.body: Ana Montana, the model and social media influencer linked to NBA star LaMelo Ball, is facing felony drug charges in North Carolina. Montana, whose real name is Analicia Chaves, was arrested Monday in Mecklenburg County, according to booking records. She faces two felony counts of obtaining a controlled substance by fraud or forgery. She also faces two misdemeanor counts of simple possession of a Schedule IV controlled substance. She was held on a $20,000 bond in connection with the felony charges.According to an arrest warrant, authorities allege Montana obtained alprazolam, the generic form of Xanax, from Walgreens using prescriptions written with a doctor’s allegedly stolen DEA registration and medical provider ID. Her lawyer has offered clarification about the allegations.Who is Ana Montana, LaMelo Ball’s baby mama?Ana Montana is the professional name of Analicia Chaves. She is a model, fashion influencer, social media personality and entrepreneur. She has built a large following online and has worked with fashion brands, including Fashion Nova.Montana has also appeared in music videos for artists such as Flo Rida and Rick Ross. Her work in fashion and social media has made her a recognised name among celebrity and influencer audiences.Away from modelling, Montana has spoken publicly about fertility and her personal IVF journey. She is also associated with the I Am Fertility Nonprofit and promotes non-toxic living through her online platforms.Montana has been linked with LaMelo Ball since around 2023. Ball is an NBA star who began his professional career with the Charlotte Hornets. The couple kept much of their relationship private, but they later became parents.They welcomed their first child together, a son named LaOne, in January 2026. His birth was publicly revealed on Mother’s Day in May 2026.Montana’s latest legal case is separate from her career in modelling and social media. The arrest warrant lists February 21 as the date of the alleged conduct. The warrant was reportedly issued on September 22, six days before her arrest.The charges centre on alprazolam prescriptions. Authorities allege the prescriptions were written using a doctor’s stolen DEA registration and medical provider identification number.Montana’s lawyer told TMZ that the allegations involve a doctor who allegedly used fraudulent credentials to prescribe the medication.“To clarify, the charges allege that a doctor who used a fraudulent DEA registration and NPI number prescribed Alprazolam for Ms. Chaves, and that she used the prescription written by the doctor to obtain the prescribed Alprazolam at a pharmacy”, he said.The lawyer also addressed the possession charges.“The drug possession charges appear to allege that she possessed the aforementioned Alprazolam upon obtaining it from the pharmacy via the prescription written by the doctor,” the lawyer added.Montana was held on a $20,000 bond related to the felony charges. articles.title: El mayor imperio del deporte
articles.standfirst: De las zapatillas a la NBA, NASCAR, la tecnología y las apuestas: cómo Michael Jordan convirtió su nombre en una máquina empresarial que, más de dos décadas después de su retirada, sigue creciendo y generando millones
articles.summary: De las zapatillas a la NBA, NASCAR, la tecnología y las apuestas: cómo Michael Jordan convirtió su nombre en una máquina empresarial que, más de dos décadas después de su retirada, sigue creciendo y generando millones
articles.body: Michael Jordan apareció este martes en Lisboa sentado entre dos de los hombres más importantes del negocio del sports betting: Carsten Koerl, CEO de Sportradar, y Jason Robins, fundador y CEO de DraftKings. No estaba allí únicamente como la leyenda de los Bulls. Jordan es inversor y asesor de Sportradar y mantiene también una participación en DraftKings. La escena resume bastante bien en qué se ha convertido Michael Jordan. A los 63 años, más de dos décadas después de su retirada, su nombre sigue apareciendo en algunos de los negocios que están transformando el deporte. Y no solo como imagen. Jordan ha pasado de vender zapatillas a tener participaciones en equipos, compañías tecnológicas, empresas de apuestas, NASCAR, restauración, tequila y coleccionismo. Su patrimonio ronda los 4.300 millones de dólares, según Forbes. Durante toda su carrera como jugador ganó unos 90 millones de dólares en salarios. De sus socios comerciales, Forbes calcula que ha recibido unos 2.400 millones antes de impuestos. Sin embargo, el gran negocio de Michael Jordan nunca fue jugar al baloncesto. Fue conseguir que Michael Jordan siguiera siendo un negocio mucho después de dejar de jugar. En 1984, Nike firmó con un Jordan de 21 años un contrato de unos 500.000 dólares anuales más royalties. Cuatro décadas después, Forbes calcula que Nike le paga cerca de 300 millones de dólares al año. La magnitud real, sin embargo, está en otro sitio. Jordan Brand generó 7.034 millones de dólares en ventas para Nike durante el ejercicio fiscal 2026, aunque cayó un 3% respecto al año anterior. No es dinero que Jordan se lleve directamente al bolsillo: es la facturación de los productos de la marca dentro de Nike. Pero sirve para entender el tamaño de la máquina que ayudó a crear. Y la máquina no se ha quedado en el baloncesto. En 2026, Jordan Brand dio otro paso: se convirtió en la primera marca de Nike que viste a una selección nacional de fútbol, después de cerrar una colaboración con Brasil para su segunda equipación y una colección de ropa urbana. El Jumpman, nacido en una pista de baloncesto, se ha instalado así en uno de los mayores escenarios del fútbol mundial. Es una de las claves para entender a Jordan. Y es que su nombre ya no depende del deporte que le hizo famoso. Jordan también aprendió que había otra manera de ganar dinero con el deporte. En 2010 compró los Charlotte Hornets. En 2023 vendió la mayoría de su participación, en una operación que valoró la franquicia en unos 3.000 millones de dólares, pero conservó una participación minoritaria. Y antes incluso de salir de Charlotte había entrado en otro deporte. En 2020 se convirtió, junto a Denny Hamlin, en propietario de 23XI Racing, equipo de NASCAR. En febrero de 2026, uno de sus coches ganó la Daytona 500, otro de esos momentos que muestran hasta dónde ha llegado el personaje. Y entonces llegó el dinero de la tecnología. Aquí es donde el imperio se vuelve todavía más interesante. Jordan no se limitó a seguir explotando su imagen. Empezó a poner dinero y reputación en negocios que estaban cambiando la industria deportiva. En Sportradar, compañía especializada en datos y tecnología deportiva, es inversor y special advisor. Aumentó su participación en 2021 y asumió entonces un papel formal de asesoramiento, especialmente en estrategia, producto y mercado estadounidense. Con DraftKings hizo algo parecido. Entró en 2020 como inversor y asesor especial del consejo a cambio de una participación accionarial, con funciones relacionadas con estrategia, producto, marketing y otras iniciativas de la compañía. Y ahí está la razón por la que su aparición de esta semana en Lisboa resulta especialmente significativa. La lista sigue. Jordan es cofundador de Cincoro Tequila, un negocio que comparte con otros grandes nombres del deporte y el entretenimiento. También ha participado en negocios vinculados a la restauración y al lujo y está detrás de Grove XXIII, su exclusivo proyecto de golf en Florida. Y hasta el mercado de las piezas históricas de Jordan sigue creciendo. Su rookie card de 1986 alcanzó en 2025 un precio de 2,7 millones de dólares en una venta privada, según Forbes.La lógica es sencilla... y aplastante. Hay quien quiere vestir Jordan. Hay quien quiere invertir en Jordan. Hay quien quiere coleccionar Jordan. Y hay quien quiere hacer negocios con Jordan. Hay una parte del imperio de Michael Jordan que no aparece en los balances. Son los millones que ha destinado a hospitales, educación, organizaciones sociales y programas para niños. Jordan ha destinado 27 millones de dólares a Novant Health, según la propia organización. El dinero ha financiado cuatro clínicas familiares para comunidades con dificultades de acceso a la sanidad y, más recientemente, un instituto de neurociencias que lleva el nombre de su madre, Deloris P. Jordan. Esta última aportación fue de 10 millones de dólares. Su relación con la organización Make-A-Wish también viene de décadas atrás. En 2023 donó 10 millones de dólares, entonces la mayor donación individual recibida por la organización, con motivo de su 60 cumpleaños. Y junto a Jordan Brand comprometió 100 millones de dólares durante diez años para apoyar organizaciones vinculadas a comunidades negras en ámbitos como educación, justicia económica y justicia social.

articles.summary: New York, donde juega Raquel Carrera, elimina al número 1, Minnesota Lynx, y se mete en semifinales
articles.body: En 30 años de historia de la WNBA, con varios cambios en los formatos de los playoffs, nunca había ocurrido lo que pasó en el Madison Square Garden, que sigue de fiesta. Las Liberty, numero 8 en temporada regular, eliminaron a las Lynx, el mejor equipo en temporada regular, tras imponerse 87-71 y poner el 2-0 a la sorprendente eliminatoria. En 2022, la WNBA cambió el formato de los playoffs. Jugaban los ocho mejores equipos clasificados de la temporada regular, independientemente de la conferencia a la que pertenecieran. Y después del cambio ha llegado la primera gran sorpresa. Sin el concurso de Raquel Carrera, que no jugó por decisión técnica, Jonquel Jones, 21 puntos y 13 rebotes, lideró a las Liberty ante un rival que había dominado el campeonato hasta llegar a las series por el anillo. Breanna Stewart contribuyó con 21 puntos y Sabrina Ionescu aportó 18 para las Liberty, que ahora esperan rival de la serie entre Mystics y Dream, que lidera Atlanta (0-1). Para los Lynx, que no han parado de recibir premios como el de mejor entrenadora del año, para Cheryl Reeve, y el de novata del año, de forma unánime, para Olivia Miles, la decepción fue terrible. "A Olivia le dije que cuándo había sido la última vez que una novata lideraba al mejor equipo. Debemos arroparla ahora", dijo la entrenadora.

articles.title: Blockbuster NBA Trade Idea To Boost a New Eastern Conference Contender
articles.summary: Domantas Sabonis and the Sacramento Kings seem ready to go their separate ways. The Toronto Raptors can help give both of them what they want.
articles.body:
Domantas Sabonis and the Sacramento Kings seem ready to go their separate ways . The Toronto Raptors can help give both of them what they want.

Between Sabonis switching agents, the Kings' overall direction and the usual onrush of various murmurings , this is a situation that'd be resolved already if not for the big man's complicated value.

The two years and $94.1 million left on his deal always felt steep. It is even steeper coming off a season in which he played just 19 games.

Even after the Kawhi Leonard trade, though, the Raptors still need a frontcourt upgrade—or at least an alternative to Collin Murray-Boyles-at-the-5 minutes. The historically durable Sabonis can be just that.

Los Angeles Clippers Receive: Pat Connaughton, Toronto's 2029 second-round pick, $3.8 million cash (via Charlotte)

Sacramento Kings Receive: Royce O'Neale, Jakob Poeltl, Tidjane Salaün, 2027 first-round pick (least favorable of Denver, L.A. Clippers, Oklahoma City and Toronto, via Toronto), Orlando's 2028 second-round pick (via Charlotte), Toronto's 2029 second-round pick, Phoenix's 2031 second-round pick (via Charlotte)

Toronto Raptors Receive: Domantas Sabonis

Out: Pat Connaughton, Royce O'Neale, Tidjane Salaün, Orlando's 2028 second-round pick, Phoenix's 2031 second-round pick, $3.8 million cash

Taking on almost $7 million in salary should faze the Hornets. They have over $22 million in room beneath the tax. Barrett adds more offensive optionality to the team. If things don't work out, he comes off the books after this season.

Toronto has generally lowered Barrett's on-ball responsibility since acquiring him from the New York Knicks. His slashing and comfort getting out in transition will never be the most efficient, but it's good enough for him to work off others, particularly given the Hornets' spacer-heavy roster construction.

Charlotte may even find it needs to ratchet up Barrett's creation workload. Coby White and Dennis Schröder usurp him in the secondary pecking order, but Kon Knueppel's hamstring injury and Brandon Miller's recovery from left shoulder surgery could eat into their availability at the start of the season.

The Hornets are also erasing two roster spots, dropping them down to 14 total. Equally important, by guaranteeing Connaughton's money as part of the deal, they are sending out enough money to preserve the entire $40.8 million LaMelo Ball traded player exception. Perhaps best of all, they're shedding $22 million in guaranteed salary from their 2027-28 payroll by going from Salaün ($10.4 million team option) and O'Neale ($11.6 million) to Barrett's expiring deal.

Punting on Salaün, two drafts removed from picking him sixth overall, admittedly isn't the greatest look. It's also borderline necessary. He delivered more encouraging stretches last season but has little chance of cracking a rotation that should see Naz Reid, Grant Williams (when healthy) and Hannes Steinbach get varying degrees of use at the 4.

In: Pat Connaughton (into minimum salary exception), Toronto's 2029 second-round pick, $3.8 million cash (via Charlotte)

The Clippers are effectively being compensated with a second-round pick to take on and then, presumably, waive Connaughton's minimum salary. With more than $15 million in room under the tax, they shouldn't flinch.

Granted, purchasing second-round picks usually won't cost an entire minimum salary. That's where the cash comes into play.

Charlotte is creating a roster spot, juicing next summer's financial flexibility and preserving the LaMelo Ball TPE as part of this mega deal. Even when adding to this season's payroll, it shouldn't mind sending out enough cash to cover the cost of Los Angeles waiving Connaughton.

In: Royce O'Neale, Jakob Poeltl, Tidjane Salaün, 2027 first-round pick, 2029 second-round pick, 2031 second-round pick

Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer previously reported that Sabonis' contract is considered a net negative around the league, but that the Kings wouldn't move him without getting actual value in return. Their best chance at accomplishing that is a package like this.

Poeltl has another four years left on his contract, but its $103 million balance is close to what Sabonis will earn over the next two seasons ($94.1 million). Working with that smaller number will open up different avenues in trades and, eventually, free agency. The final season on Poeltl's deal is also, as of now, only guaranteed for $5 million .

This draft haul won't blow anyone away. Still, the Kings are unlikely to do better. Sabonis could ball out to start the year. Teams would still view his cap-sheet number and proximity to another deal as a deterrent.

Grabbing an extra first, some seconds and a flier on Salaün is within the realm of reasonable. O'Neale has $11.6 million owed to him in 2027-28 and has slipped considerably on defense. As someone who's shooting over 39 percent from three since 2022 on nearly eight attempts per 36 minutes, Sacramento should still be able to get something for him down the line.

The Kings can rework the terms if they want RJ Barrett, but this structure does more to lean out the immediate payroll. Sacramento has no business being the team that pays Barrett next summer.

Out: RJ Barrett, Jakob Poeltl, 2027 first-round pick, 2029 second-round pick

Consolidating Barrett and Poeltl into Sabonis is not without risk. Crafting a top-tier defense around him is a massive undertaking.

It just so happens that the Raptors have the personnel to do it.

Scottie Barnes, Kawhi Leonard, Collin Murray-Boyles and Jamal Shead provide top-tier coverage for him. For all his flaws, Sabonis is generally a dominant defensive rebounder—an area where Toronto hasn't ranked higher than 16th since 2016.

Offloading Barrett does leave the Raptors more vulnerable to a Leonard injury. Yet Sabonis' work as an offensive hub is its own insulation for Kawhi's absence. Moving Barrett also chisels out extra reps for Ja'Kobe Walter, Allen Graves and Jamison Battle. Toronto could make far riskier gambles.

Sabonis' contract is a thorny financial fit alongside deals for Barnes, Leonard and Immanuel Quickley. Still, it comes off the books two years sooner than Poeltl's pact—just before the Raptors have to worry about Murray-Boyles' inevitable rookie extension kicking in.

On top of that, Toronto is shedding more than enough money to duck back below the tax . That's breathing room it will appreciate closer to the trade deadline.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Details emerge in incident between Aces star A'ja Wilson and Fever fan during playoff game
articles.summary: A'ja Wilson confronted a courtside fan during the Indiana Fever vs Aces WNBA playoff game, but arena security cleared the man of any conduct violation.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark put together a historic performance as the Indiana Fever cruised to a 99-89 victory in Game 2 of their playoff matchup against the Aces on Tuesday, forcing a win-or-go-home Game 3 in Las Vegas. The biggest story is what happened off the court, though. With four minutes left in the game, A'ja Wilson drew a controversial blocking foul on Sophie Cunningham. She then saw a fan sitting a few rows back in the baseline courtside seats and took exception with him pointing and saying something to her. She then went out of her way to go two rows deep into the crowd to confront the fan, who had since sat down. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Amazon Prime Video broadcasters all considered the male Fever fan guilty before details of what actually happened came out, scolding him on air for his behavior. They had no facts to back up their claims and pronounced Wilson a victim of unsportsmanlike fan behavior as the man was escorted from his seats by security. The fan was quickly deemed innocent by the Fever saying, "Following a report of a comment directed toward a player, arena security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses. Security determined there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct, the fan was not removed from the arena. We consider the matter closed." A fan sitting next to the man involved in the confrontation with Wilson shared details with OutKick about the incident. According to the fan, the man simply said: "It (the foul) is on you!" while pointing at Wilson. The fan also said that Wilson kept yelling, "You don't point at me!" That’s it. Nothing sexist. Nothing race-related. No profanity. Just a fan being a fan. Wilson was set off by a fan sitting courtside, who believed the blocking foul to be a charge. Oh, the horror! The fan also told OutKick when the man returned to his seat minutes later, he received "thunderous applause" and was "high-fiving other fans." Wilson even admitted postgame that her confrontation with the fan wasn't because she was offended by what he said, but that his action of taking a half step forward toward the court was "unacceptable." "If I see a man stepping towards me, I don’t give a damn what you said … That’s unacceptable," she said. The fan also refuted the claims that the ejected fan was "coming at her." He said, "He was not obnoxious or louder than anyone else. There was never any sense of "coming at her." He was seated by the time she was near him." He also mentioned that the fan was escorted out quickly because "the Aces were so adamant he left." WNBA SILENCE ON DIJONAI CARRINGTON'S 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' POST EXPOSES SANDY BRONDELLO DOUBLE STANDARD According to Rule 12A, Section V: Any player, coach, or trainer who deliberately enters the spectator stands during a game will be automatically ejected. The rulebook also explicitly states that the first row of seats is considered the beginning of the spectator stands. Wilson's actions seem to have warranted an ejection by the letter of the law. This was just another unnecessary fan incident involving a Fever supporter that was ejected and then proven innocent. It's happened multiple times this season alone. Aces' Jackie Young had two male Fever fans escorted from their seats at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. They were both proven innocent by arena security, just like the fan from Game 2 Tuesday. Also, Amazon Prime was covering that game and the broadcasters considered the men guilty before proven innocent. This is just another mess for the WNBA, a terrible look for A'ja Wilson, and wildly unprofessional from Amazon Prime Video.

articles.title: Lexie Brown singles out Caitlin Clark trait that will make her ‘one of the best point guards to ever play in the WNBA’
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark has already cemented herself as one of the best players in the WNBA this year, but she is now being backed to be one of the top point guards in...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has already cemented herself as one of the best players in the WNBA this year, but she is now being backed to be one of the top point guards in history.

Clark ended the 2026 regular season with the most total points created in the entire league, and most recently impressed for the Indiana Fever in game two of their first-round playoff series.

She made history when she scored 27 points and provided 15 assists in the win over the Las Vegas Aces .

Elsewhere, Lexie Brown has suggested that Clark's court vision can help her 'go down as one of the best point guards to ever play in the WNBA'.

Lexie Brown praises Caitlin Clark's court vision

In a clip shared by NBA TV on X/Twitter, Brown said: "For me, I've said this since she was at Iowa when she was a freshman.

"I remember watching her and just saying, seeing her court vision, the way she finds her teammates, the way her head is always up when she's advancing the ball, finding the open man in transition in the half-court.

"I think, I don't know if it's underrated, because she's breaking all of these records.

"But what I'm saying like, she can go down as one of the best point guards to ever play in the WNBA.

"Like, she's well on her way already. So for me, that's been, yes her scoring ability is incredible, but for me, one of the things I've always loved about her game is her court vision."

Clark finished the regular season with 333 assists, which was the second-most in the league behind Alyssa Thomas .

And so far, her 25 assists in this year's playoffs put her well ahead of all competition in the postseason, with Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young joint-second in the standings with 15 at the time of writing.

Yahoo Sports AM is our daily newsletter that keeps you up to date on all things sports. Sign up here to get it every weekday morning.

The MLB postseason kicked off on Tuesday, and while these four series are far from over, history suggests the Braves, White Sox , Yankees and Padres are in very good shape.

15-1: Since the best-of-three Wild Card Round was introduced in 2022, Game 1 winners have gone on to win 15 of the 16 series . The lone exception? Last year's Yankees, who rallied to win Games 2 and 3 against the Red Sox . Can Boston return the favor this year?

Braves 5, Phillies 3: Atlanta trailed 3-2 with two on and two outs in the bottom of the eighth when Austin Riley — who's endured the worst season of his career (.654 OPS) — came to the plate. One pitch later he played the hero, hitting a game-winning, three-run homer to completely change the narrative of his disappointing campaign.

It can't have hurt that the White Sox received a letter before the game from their most famous fan, as Pope Leo XIV invoked "the Almighty's abundant blessings" upon team owner Jerry Reinsdorf.

Yankees 9, Red Sox 0: No Aaron Judge , no problem. After their ailing captain was left off the Wild Card roster, the Yanks got everything they needed and more from presumptive AL Cy Young Cam Schlittler (6.1 IP, 10 K, 2 H) and lefty slugger Ben Rice (4-5, 2 HR, 6 RBI), who capped off the rout with a grand slam that electrified Yankee Stadium.

Padres 8, Cubs 0: San Diego ended the season as the hottest team in baseball and clearly lost no momentum as the playoffs began, dominating the Cubs behind a masterpiece from Michael King (7 IP, 8 K, 1 H) — who took a no-hitter into the seventh inning — and home runs from Fernando Tatis Jr , Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts .

What to watch: All four Game 2's are today, as the Phillies , Astros, Red Sox and Cubs will attempt to keep their seasons alive and force a decisive Game 3.

🎓 COLLEGE SPORTS ARE ONE STEP CLOSER TO PROTECTIVE CUSTODY

Politicians on both sides of the Senate aisle have declared their overwhelming belief that college sports require protection from Congress. But theirs is only one vote of support in a process that could become even more turbulent.

ICYMI: The Protect College Sports Act passed the Senate on Monday night , with remarkably bipartisan support delivering a lopsided 77-22 vote in favor.

What does it say: The bill aims to codify long-term solutions to the myriad hot-button issues that have sown chaos across the college sports landscape.

Revenue-share cap: On top of the approximately $21 million in revenue sharing allowed under the House settlement, schools will have an additional $22.5 million retention fund for existing players and a $5 million pool for women's and non-revenue sports.

Third parties: Multimedia rights companies and third parties (i.e. apparel sponsors) must certify that the school did not fund NIL compensation for athletes, nor negotiate or determine the amount paid to athletes.

Eligibility: Codifies the NCAA's policy allowing athletes to compete for five calendar years beginning at the sooner of the date of enrollment or the start of the academic year following the athlete's 19th birthday.

Transfers: Undergraduate athletes can transfer only once without sitting out a year (graduate students can transfer without delay). All players can transfer without restriction if, for example, there is a head coaching change or their school discontinues their sport.

Antitrust exemption: The NCAA receives a limited antitrust exemption to enforce the compensation, transfer, and eligibility rules.

Conference expansion: Power conferences can't expand beyond 20 schools, and schools must go independent for three years before switching conferences. The latter provision sunsets in six years (conveniently coinciding with the expiration of existing media deals).

Media rights: Schools can pool their media rights, provided 75% of FBS schools agree to participate. This cannot happen until existing deals expire.

Coaches: Coaches cannot change jobs mid-season, though they can accept a new job. An amendment to cap their compensation and further restrict their movement failed.

Don't bet the House: The bill now moves to the House, where there is abundant uncertainty both about the timing of a vote and the prospects of passage. A vote is unlikely before the midterms, and results at the ballot box could impact the appetite for one. As one Democratic House staff member told Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger: "That bill is dead."

We're roughly one-quarter of the way through the college football season, and thus far three players stand above the rest as favorites for the Heisman Trophy.

Jeremiah Smith (WR, Ohio State): The Buckeyes junior is the betting favorite (+275), leading the nation in receiving yards (617) and touchdowns (7), while ranking fourth in receptions (33).

On Saturday he became the fifth player in Big Ten history with at least 3,000 career receiving yards and 30 receiving touchdowns, and he's on pace to break Jaxon Smith-Njigba's school record for receiving yards in a season (1,606 in 2021).

If he keeps up this pace, he could become the fifth wide receiver* ever to win the Heisman, and just the second in the past 35 years.

Darian Mensah (QB, Miami ): The sensational signal-caller (+400) has been worth every penny Miami gave him to transfer from Duke, throwing for 1,211 yards and an FBS-best 14 touchdowns against zero interceptions for the fourth-ranked Hurricanes.

How's this for a wild stat: He's thrown more touchdowns (14) than incompletions (12), becoming the first FBS player to do that through four games in the last 30 years.

Kamario Taylor (QB, Mississippi State): The first two players were expected to be near the top of this list, but Taylor (+700) has elbowed his way into the race with four otherworldly games after opening the season at 150-1.

The 6-foot-4 gunslinger has thrown for 1,192 yards and 14 touchdowns (tied with Mensah atop the leaderboard) against just two interceptions, while adding 185 yards and a score on the ground, too.

Last year as a true freshman he was the backup on a team that went 5-8; now he's the starter for the undefeated Bulldogs, who at No. 16 are ranked for the first time since 2022.

articles.body:
Joel Embiid is probably excited to start the new NBA season. The Philadelphia 76ers are more stacked than ever after acquiring LeBron James and Jaylen Brown this offseason.

During the Philadelphia 76ers ' Media Day, Embiid spoke about teaming up with James, with whom he won an Olympic gold medal in 2024, and Brown , whom he faced in the first round of last season's NBA playoffs.

"People who know me know that the one thing I care about the most is winning… That's the one thing that sticks out: I want to win, and I will do whatever it takes to win. That was a great time being on that Olympic team, but I think it comes down to the fit. He's one of the best, has a high basketball IQ, so we kind of see the game the same way," Embiid said of James via The Athletic's Mike Vorkunov.

"All those battles against Boston all those years, the one thing I get playing against him is how competitive he is. You won't find too many guys in this league who are able to play two sides of the floor at a high level," he added about Brown. "A good example is Game 7 vs. Boston when we made our comeback. None of the guys could stop me, and he knew he couldn't stop me anyway, but he decided to take the challenge."

Philadelphia 76ers News: LeBron James opens up on the team's potential challenges this upcoming season

In a recent episode of the Mind the Game podcast, LeBron James urged the Philadelphia 76ers to adopt a "bunker mentality" to block the outside noise throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

"You know, you got your group chat with your boys, and like, 'Man, you know, you got 11 shots last night. You should have 15. Why Bron ain't pass the ball more? Why Joe ain't pass the ball more? Tyrese, oh, you on the wing. What, VJ taking too many step-backs? Why he take you out?' It's gonna be all that type of s" James explained. "It's been happening my whole career. The only thing that matters is what we preach every day and how we're gonna hold each other accountable."

"If we can do that, if we can preach that, we can practice that, because it's gonna be tested. If we can practice and preach it every day, then we'll give ourselves the best possible chance, along with health, obviously, which is very important, probably the most important in sports," he concluded.

articles.body:
Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) on Tuesday blasted Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.) after he and his staff appeared to confuse one basketball team for another when questioning former special counsel Jack Smith about his attendance at a game.

Schmitt earlier Tuesday asked Smith if he attended a February 2024 NBA game in Atlanta between the Hawks and the Golden State Warriors. The inquiry and subsequent exchange drew in other senators and sparked confusion after he appeared to mistake the Iowa Hawkeyes for the Atlanta Hawks.

“Look, nobody ever heard of Sen. Schmitt before, and nobody’s going to ever hear of him again,” Raskin, the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, told CNN’s Erin Burnett. “He’s basically disgraced himself and identified himself with this ridiculous little stunt where he thought he was going to perform some major service to Donald Trump.”

Raskin added that Schmitt’s questioning was “all about being the most obsequious sycophant you can be, and he proved that he was.”

“And he doesn’t even understand how much that he’s utterly humiliated himself in the eyes of the country,” he added.

Burnett asked if Schmitt will apologize to Smith for the mix-up, to which Raskin answered, “Well, not from the looks of it.” Smith at first denied attending the game before Schmitt’s staff displayed a poster of texts of the ex-federal prosecutor’s staff discussing seat numbers, and Schmitt said “for context” the date of the game was just after Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis (D) acknowledged a romance with a colleague, an incident that shook up the 2020 election interference case in Georgia against President Trump. The former special counsel’s demeanor changed to confusion as he denied what Schmitt accused him of, saying he attended an Iowa Hawkeyes game in Maryland to watch Caitlin Clark play. Footage of the game , where he was spotted in the crowd, has since circulated on social media. Schmitt concluded his questioning, after lawmakers pushed back over the specifics of the two teams, by calling Smith a “dirtbag” and a “villain.” Senate Democrats accused the Missouri Republican of airing a conspiracy theory, but the senator has gone on to promote the inquiry on conservative media. Nonpartisan outlets also questioned him about the gaffe, including Nexstar affiliate KTVI St. Louis. Schmitt defended himself , saying his job is “to ask the questions, and his job is to answer the questions.” As to whether or not he believed Smith perjured himself, Schmitt has said “we’ll see.” Sen. articles.title: Aces star A'ja Wilson gets into heated exchange with fan in Game 2 loss to Fever: 'That is unacceptable'
articles.summary: A'ja Wilson was livid and had to be held back from the fan sitting underneath the basket at Gainbridge Fieldhouse.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson got into it with a fan sitting at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Tuesday late in their Game 2 loss to the Indiana Fever .

And she did not hold back on the man after the game, either.

"I've never seen A'ja Wilson go like that," Aces head coach Becky Hammon said after their 99-89 loss. "So whatever was done, I can tell you she felt very disrespected in that moment. I've never seen her really react like that, ever."

Wilson was trying to fight through a screen set by Sophie Cunningham midway through the fourth quarter in Indianapolis when the two got tangled up. Cunningham was sent down to the court hard, and was called for a foul.

But as Wilson was walking down the lane after play had stopped, she suddenly erupted at a fan sitting behind the basket. Wilson had to be pulled back by several teammates and officials. It's unclear what was actually said by the fan to spark the exchange, but Wilson was livid.

The fan was removed from his seat briefly, but returned soon after and was spotted celebrating with people sitting around him, according to Fever reporter Tony East .

"If I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don't give a damn what you said. I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable," Wilson said after the game. "You don't know me to step toward me and point at me. I'm not for that s*** at all … That there is unacceptable. How he gets back in the game because they said he didn't do anything, of course he did."

After a lengthy review, Wilson was assessed a technical foul and Cunningham was called for a personal foul. Kelsey Mitchell missed the free throw for the Fever, while Wilson hit both of hers. That made it a nine-point game with 4:10 left in the contest.

Wilson said that she apologized to her team for the technical foul, but she's not sorry for her actions.

"It's just certain things that I'm not going to allow anymore, because it's unacceptable," she said. "You don't know me at all to come and step toward me and point at me and say anything."

The Fever released a statement on the incident after the game, saying they are not going to investigate the matter further. The fan in question, they said, did not violate their rules and was allowed to return.

"Following a report of a comment directed toward a player, arena security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses," the team said, via The Athletic's James Boyd . "Security determined there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct, the fan was not removed from the arena. We consider the matter closed."

After the chaos, the Fever held on down the stretch to grab the 10-point win . That tied the series up and forced a deciding Game 3 on Thursday night in Las Vegas . The winner will advance into the semifinals.

Caitlin Clark had 27 points and 15 assists to lead the Fever while shooting 9-of-18 from the field. Kelsey Mitchell added 26 points, and Aliyah Boston finished with 22 points. Jackie Young led the Aces with 31 points in the loss, and Wilson finished with 22 points and nine rebounds.

Wilson averaged 26.2 points and 9.4 rebounds per game this season, her ninth in the league. The four-time MVP, who has won the award in back-to-back seasons now, is widely considered the favorite to win the award again this season.

While things got heated in Indianapolis, Wilson will have a much friendlier crowd for the winner-take-all Game 3 on Thursday. A fan interaction like she had on Tuesday shouldn't be something she has to worry about.

"You don't have to like me, you don't have to love me," she said. "You can hate me with all your heart. But you don't know me. "But I guarantee you will respect me."

articles.title: Caitlin Clark keeps Fever's season alive with fiery, historic performance in Game 2 vs. Aces: 'She was the catalyst'
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark said the Fever's mantra in Game 2 was "don't be soft." Mission accomplished.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — The scenes 48 hours and 1,849 miles apart were stark. In the first, a morose Caitlin Clark covered her face with a towel draped over her head, her words sharp and direct in attacking a performance her head coach said humbled them . Two days later, Clark beams amid the bright Gainbridge Fieldhouse lights once more, interjecting when someone mentions her fiery competitiveness.

"You think?" she laughs, eyes alight, praise and talking points ready after a 99-89 win over the Las Vegas Aces in Game 2 of the WNBA playoffs first round on Tuesday night.

Clark will not say how ticked off she was by a Game 1 blowout that put the backs of the championship-aspiring Indiana Fever to the wall. What she will do is point out that she hit three shots in a row after the officiating crew called her for a technical foul less than two minutes into the second quarter.

On a night she said the referees struggled — a claim neither side of the court disagreed with — she said she respected the referees for calling it.

Yes, she said, she definitely deserved it. No, she answers, she didn't do it on purpose. No doubt, though, that it further lit a necessary fire.

"We didn't have the mentality [in Game 1] of coming in, kind of puffing our chests a little bit, and I think tonight we really had that," Clark said after sticking hers out with 27 points, 15 assists and 7 rebounds.

The MVP candidate credited Myisha Hines-Allen for the pregame prompting. In the later minutes of the first quarter, Hines-Allen dusted up with Aces center and Game 1 superstar A'ja Wilson, to which Sophie Cunningham waved her hands up to hear from a raucous home crowd, and Clark slapped her singular championship-winning vet's hands.

"That's what we talked about as a team is like, don't be soft," Clark said. "We kind of beat ourselves in that way."

A minute later, Clark reached in on Wilson and ripped the ball to force a jump ball. With every centimeter of movement, the series wrested from the grasp of Wilson to that of Clark. Now it goes back to Las Vegas tied 1-1, and everyone's season is on the line.

"It's about getting hit, but understanding like, listen, we gotta get back up," Aliyah Boston told Yahoo Sports. "You cannot just lay there."

They called it a bounce-back. The intentionality was as clear as the mood shift. In the locker room, head coach Stephanie White drew up the first play to key open Clark on the perimeter. White told everyone she was going to make it.

"I was just trying not to let everybody down because we were all visualizing that I was going to make it, so I needed to get the night started off right," Clark said.

It officially clocked in at 29 feet, a mere 15 seconds into the contest. An early trademark 3 portends a good night for Clark, and Game 2 didn't disappoint. She drew contact for another three points at the free-throw line, thought an ensuing 27-footer would fall ("it just rolled out," she noted), and used the attention to feed Makayla Timpson and Boston on cuts inside an open paint.

Boston finished through contact around Wilson, nearly pristine in her attack and movements, for 22 points on 15 attempts. Kelsey Mitchell did her work as usual, scoring 26 with a sharp 3 of 4 line from the perimeter. Everyone who played scored. They shot a combined 52.1%.

"We just had a presence about us right from the start of the game," Clark said.

Though the Fever looked to be back in business, the deficit grew to eight by the first quarter's end. Jewell Loyd 's 3-pointer to open the second frame sent it to 11.

The Aces, who have only lost a series to the New York Liberty in the playoffs over the last four years, ran over the Fever in Game 1 with a proper sense of understood urgency and desperation. They knew what to expect, knew how to handle it, and operated accordingly.

White described her team as young in that area before the series began, and they swiftly proved the point. An unraveling began in the second quarter the first time around. When the initial thread began to come apart this time, they didn't let it snowball.

Composure, Boston said, was paramount. Except, well, you know.

"She's just a passionate player," Boston said, laughing at hearing that White and the coaching staff's focus was keeping Clark calm following the technical.

The whistle of Clark's first postseason tech blew in a nine-point deficit. She knows how many consecutive baskets she hit afterward: three. Not including a missed 3-pointer. Also not included: a feed to Boston in the paint, where they tore through the Aces in the first half to a tune of 30-16.

Another 3 drew the Fever within a possession, eliciting a roar from the crowd and a timeout by the Aces. They fell behind by six when Mitchell, the league's second-highest scorer, took a turn. Her running alley-oop off an Aces turnover and Clark assist gave the Fever a lead.

Clark became the first player in postseason history with at least 10 points and 10 assists in a half, setting the mark for most assists with 11. She had 14 points when the Fever led 48-43 at the half. Combined with Mitchell's 12 and Boston's eight, their big three contributed 70% of the scoring. The Aces' trio of A'ja Wilson (10 points), Chelsea Gray (10) and Jackie Young (7) had 27 of 43 in the first half.

"I mean, a double-double in the first half? Pretty incredible," White said. "The way that she moved the ball and attacked from multiple positions. You always expect her to be able to make shots and to facilitate, but I thought how she managed the game was really good and her defensive energy, I thought, was terrific."

The Fever leveled up the Aces in the physicality department, suffocating Wilson into attempting zero field goals in the third quarter. She finished with 22 points, largely rendered ineffective. Jackie Young brought the Aces back into it with a 31-point performance that wasn't enough to make up for 10 points by Gray, and single digits elsewhere.

Clark, meanwhile, shone — though the drawback of such fiery, un-soft approach did rear its head. She fouled out with 2:45 to go when she stepped into the block, attempting to stop a solo Wilson from an easy bucket.

The Fever challenged to no avail. A nervousness settled around the crowd, unsure if losing their attack-mode superstar would unspool a 92-83 lead. Mitchell lay in her trademark finger-roll, Boston drove in. Lexie Hull rebounded two key Aces misses, and Cunningham hit two free throws.

Clark said she intends to "keep my head a little bit more" in the next game, aware that one point could be the difference. The Fever need her on the floor, and at her best.

"She was the catalyst for us here tonight," White said. "And I think she's going to just take it to another level when we go to Game 3."

The fire has to travel. Or else the scene reverses itself again.

articles.title: Warriors' Steph Curry Provides Health Update After Knee Injury Derailed 2025-26 NBA Season
articles.summary: Stephen Curry is optimistic about the state of his knee following the Golden State Warriors' first training camp practice on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry is optimistic about the state of his knee following the Golden State Warriors' first training camp practice on Tuesday.

Speaking to reporters afterward, Curry explained that figuring out the issues last season allowed him and the team to put together a plan early in the offseason that should help keep him on the court:

"Last year was pretty drastic. Once I started to feel something in my knee, it was new. And by the time it had presented itself, it was kind of too late to manage it. So at that point, you're kind of chasing it in the middle of the season, and that's why it took so long to heal. This year, knowing what it is, taking advantage of the summer, having a very detailed plan to build my body, the foundation, give my knee a rest and still be prepared for training camp, that was the biggest win I've felt so far."

One change Curry pointed out was "less is more" in terms of his workouts. He's not necessarily working out less than he used to, but changing the types of things he did in ways that didn't put as much stress on his legs:

"That doesn't mean you don't work as hard. You just work different in the sense of how much you're on your feet. … I did a lot of underwater treadmill stuff to keep my aerobic capacity but not have the pounding on my joints. So you're just working different, even though the volume of work was pretty much the same. And then in the tail end of the summer, you're able to safely kind of ramp up."

Curry was limited to just 43 games last season primarily due to soreness in his right knee that lingered. He said in April after missing 27 straight games it wasn't a structural issue with the knee.

"There's nothing structurally wrong with my knee," Curry explained. "So it's not like I'm compromised out there. It is a new normal, though, if that makes sense."

It will be interesting to see how, if at all, Curry tries adjusting his style of play to account for the knee. As recently as the 2024-25 season, he was running on average 2.4 miles per game.

Curry is famous for being in constant motion during games to create space and wear down opposing defenders. He is now 38 years old and admitted Tuesday that you "got to be a little bit more patient" even though he feels strong.

The 43 games Curry played during the 2025-26 campaign were his fewest in an 82-game season. He was still dominant when he did play, averaging 26.6 points on 39.3 percent three-point shooting and 4.7 assists per contest.

Golden State finished 37-45, marking its first time under .500 since 2019-20 (15-50). The Warriors didn't make any significant additions to the roster via free agency, so the health of Curry, Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis and Draymond Green will determine their ceiling this season.

Porziņģis is out indefinitely due to an unspecified health issue. Butler is doing light on-court work in his recovery from a torn ACL. Yaxel Lendeborg, the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft, could get a lot of run early in the season depending on how long they are without Porziņģis and Butler.

Curry is still good enough to make the Warriors a playoff contender in a deep Western Conference, as long as he can avoid extended absences that robbed him of so much time last season.

Sunday might offer the first glimpse of how Curry's knee looks when the Warriors tipoff their preseason schedule against the Houston Rockets in Hawaii.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Jalen Duren Weight Clause Amid Pistons' $200M Contract Offer
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons have sent a fully guaranteed five-year, $200 million contract offer to center and restricted free agent Jalen Duren.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons have sent a fully guaranteed five-year, $200 million contract offer to center and restricted free agent Jalen Duren.

Rumors circulated via Hunter Patterson and Sam Amick of The Athletic that the offer included a weight clause "requiring Duren to check his weight monthly throughout the calendar year." The duo clarified the clause was not in writing.

However, Amick and Patterson reported Wednesday that the weight clause "is no longer part of the talks."

"Per league sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity as negotiations continue, the weight clause initially proposed as part of the Pistons' five-year, $200 million offer is no longer part of the talks. The clause was never put in writing. That $200 million offer, which Duren has thus far not accepted, is fully guaranteed and includes no weight-related provisions."

The Athletic gave more insight into the weight clause amid the initial report.

"His struggles in the 2026 postseason are an obvious factor in these talks, but league sources said the perception that the Pistons believe his weight was partly to blame came as a surprise to Duren and his camp. That claim came internally after Detroit's Game 7 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers in the second round, with league sources saying the organization privately wanted Duren to cut weight then."

Duren and the Pistons are amid a lengthy contract standoff, but a massive Thursday (11:59 p.m. ET) deadline looms on the Pistons' one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer to the center. Duren, in theory, could sign that offer and then take his chances as an unrestricted free agent next season. However, as Arthur Hill of Hoops Rumors noted, Detroit could extend the deadline. That being said, Duren would remain an RFA if the QO expires.

The Sacramento Kings and Milwaukee Bucks have interest in Duren should Detroit consider the sign-and-trade route, per Chris Mannix of Sports Illustrated.

"Here's what it will take: Money, and more of it than the $200 million the Pistons are reportedly willing to pay Duren over the next five seasons. Clearly, Duren and his representatives believe there is more cash out there. Sacramento and Milwaukee have interest in Duren, a source confirmed, and likely would plus-up the offer if Detroit was willing to play ball on a sign-and-trade."

The 22-year-old Duren earned All-Star and All-NBA Third Team honors last season after averaging 19.5 points on 65.0 percent shooting and 10.5 rebounds. Detroit dominated the regular season with 60 wins, good enough for first in the Eastern Conference playoffs.

However, Duren struggled in the playoffs, which ended with the Pistons falling to the Cleveland Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference semifinals. Duren averaged 10.5 points on 51.4 percent shooting and 8.5 boards per game.

Now the waiting game continues regarding Duren's status. In the meantime, the Pistons have started training camp without the big man as they hope to build off last year and make a deeper postseason run.

articles.title: New Anthony Davis Trade Rumors Link Wizards Star to Pistons Amid Jalen Duren Contract Buzz
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards' reported reluctance to consider trading Anthony Davis could apparently change if the Detroit Pistons decide to shop Jalen Duren.
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards' reported reluctance to consider trading Anthony Davis could apparently change if the Detroit Pistons decide to shop Jalen Duren.

The Athletic's Sam Amick and Hunter Patterson reported Wednesday "league sources... confirmed an ESPN report indicating that the Washington Wizards would have interest in a Duren-for-Anthony Davis trade."

That potential deal "does not appear to be of interest to the Pistons," Amick and Patterson noted.

ESPN's Marc J. Spears said Monday on NBA Today the Wizards had "interested in a potential sign-and-trade" involving Duren, a restricted free agent who has yet to re-sign with the Pistons.

The Pistons have offered Duren a five-year, fully-guaranteed $200 million contract he has until just before midnight Thursday to accept, per Amick and Patterson.

That remains below the maximum possible offer the team could have made of $287 million over five years.

Duren could also sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer with an eye on testing free agency next summer, Amick and Patterson noted.

Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said Monday he is expecting Duren to remain with the Pistons regardless of what decision he makes regarding his next contract.

Even if the Pistons due try to trade Duren, the Wizards would reportedly have competition for a potential deal. The Sacramento Kings and Milwaukee Bucks are also interested in a potential Duren sign-and-trade, per Amick and Patterson.

These obstacles could indicate the Wizards will end up sticking with Davis, for whom they were reportedly not listening to trade offers as of June 30, per Spears .

Spears reported at the time a rival team executive said Wizards general manager Will Dawkins was a "huge fan" of Davis.

Davis is signed through next season at a $58.5 million cap hit with a player option for 2027-28. He is eligible for a four-year, $275 million extension, the first year of which would replace the player option.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported in August the Wizards and Davis were delaying contract extension talks until around 20 games into the regular season because of lingering questions regarding both Davis' health and the Wizards' hopes of contending.

Should Duren take the Pistons' qualifying offer and head into the season on an expiring contract, and should the Wizards not finalize an extension with Davis, these two teams could be potential trade partners to keep an eye on ahead of the deadline next February.
